- [x] Analysis: requirements-generator comparison (Architect vs regular LLM)
  - Date: 2026-05-21
  - What changed: Ran a controlled head-to-head on the same idea (ShelfSense). Architect: 253-char idea → 13,742 words / 108,442 chars (~23 pages, 7 chapters), 429× explosion. Regular (gpt-4o-mini, 1 call, max_tokens 16,000): 1,068-char prompt → 1,450 words / 10,580 chars (~2 pages), and only 24% of the requested 6,000 words. Architect is 10.2× the size. Key findings: single-call LLM self-limits well below its token cap; the Architect's chunked per-chapter generation (≥1,750 words/chapter, retried) is what reaches depth; the Architect ignores the questionnaire (built from idea only) while the regular path is the only one that uses it.
  - Verification: report `docs/REQUIREMENTS_GENERATOR_COMPARISON.html`; raw `docs/doc-comparison/{metrics.json,architect.md,regular.md}`.
  - Notes: Recommendations — basic workflow: regular path (tailored/fast/cheap) but add a 2-pass section-expand to fix the length shortfall; full system: Architect; and feed the questionnaire INTO the Architect so its 23 pages match what the user actually selected.

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `scripts/compareDocGenerators.js` + `scripts/buildDocComparisonReport.js` + `docs/REQUIREMENTS_GENERATOR_COMPARISON.html` | New: controlled doc-generator comparison (fetches Architect doc + generates a regular-LLM doc for the same idea, job-only/not saved) + report generator + report (2026-05-21) |

- [x] Fix: activateProject no longer marks a 0-capability build-out as activated
  - Date: 2026-05-21
  - What changed: `activateProject()` clustered requirements in a swallowed try/catch and then unconditionally set `activated=true` — so when clustering failed/returned nothing (observed on run3's ~100KB Architect doc) the user got a "ready" project with 0 capabilities after a ~15-min wait. Now: clustering retries once if it yields 0 capabilities, and if it's still 0 the function throws (project left un-activated) instead of marking it complete. Callers (`POST /setup/activate`, `architect-status`) record the failure and can retry.
  - Verification: backend `tsc --noEmit` passes; deployed to prod; functional activate confirmed still produces capabilities + activates normally.
  - Notes: The retry alone fixes the observed transient run3 case (a manual re-trigger had populated it); the throw is the safety net so an empty build-out is never presented as success.

- [x] Three operator-flagged issues from Lead Ingestion BP detail review (BPs tab + Components tab on portal)
  - Date: 2026-05-22
  - What changed: Operator opened the Lead Ingestion BP modal on `/portal/project/system?tab=bps&layer=backend` and reported three things: (1) the "Learn about this BP" chip strip + per-step "Ask Cory" links were INVISIBLE even though the operator was `ali@colaberry.com`, contradicting the prior session's review HTML; (2) the walkthrough cards suggested "Generate the backend prompt" for a backend already marked "In place (forming)" — button verb said GENERATE while the copy said EXTEND, plus steps never went away when the layer was fully done; (3) the BPs tab and Components tab displayed the same B/F/A layer state with different visual vocabularies — gray vs red for missing, icons vs text badges. Three commits, executed in order (`b0b13c7c`, `57881bf4`, `c25321d0`):
    1. **`b0b13c7c` — Cory portal gate fallback.** Root cause of (1): the `useCoryAvailable` hook only consulted `useAdminUser`, which reads `admin_token` and hits `/api/admin/me`. On `/portal/*` routes the operator authenticates via `participant_token`; if `admin_token` is missing or expired, the gate returns `false` even for authorized identities. Fix: `useCoryAvailable` now also decodes the `participant_token` JWT claims client-side (base64url payload, no signature verification — server still enforces auth on every API call) and accepts the same identity predicate (`email==ali@colaberry.com OR role==super_admin`) from either token source. Caveat documented in the hook's doc-block: the actual Cory chat (`coryApi.ts`) still calls `/api/admin/intelligence/cory` with `admin_token`, so a portal-only operator with no `admin_token` will see the chip strip render but the chat call will 401 — that's a separate auth-scope question, not this commit's scope.
    2. **`57881bf4` — Walkthrough state-aware labels + step suppression.** Audited `bpStepWalkthrough.ts`: `ctaLabel` was a static string ("Generate X prompt") regardless of layer state, while `whatItDoes` + `whyItMatters` correctly switched to "extend" language when the layer was partial. Mixed signal. Steps also never suppressed when a layer was fully present (only the agent step had a suppression rule, and only at confirmedAgents≥3 + matLevel≥4). Now: `ctaLabel` is "Generate X prompt" for missing, "Extend X prompt" for partial. Step suppressed entirely when `usability === 'ready'/'present' AND unmatched requirements === 0`. Page-kind caps still always render their upgrade step (a page is always improvable). Backend `/prompt` endpoint dispatch unchanged — the `step.key` enum is preserved so this is purely UI prose + suppression.
    3. **`c25321d0` — Visual parity across BPs and Components tabs.** Reversed the 2026-05-20 intentional divergence ("BPs asks 'what's present?', Components asks 'is it wired?'") in favor of operator mental-model consistency. `bpSignals.ts` `PILLAR_TONES.missing` collapsed from red (#b91c1c) to gray (#9ca3af) — both tabs now use the same palette. Extracted `BuiltnessIcon` + `deriveBuiltnessProps(bp)` helper into a new shared file `BPBuiltnessIcon.tsx`. `BPDomainSurfaceRows.tsx` dropped its local `PILLAR_TONES` shadow + the no-op `.map()` that re-applied it; `CapabilityGrid.tsx` dropped its inline "Built / Wired / Partial / Not built yet" text badge in favor of the shared icon. Card left-border tonal accent in CapabilityGrid still uses `bpBuiltness` for color choice — unchanged. Trade-off: loses the "red = needs work" cue in Components tab; gains one vocabulary across both surfaces.
  - Verification: frontend `npx tsc --noEmit` exit 0; CRA production build (`CI=true npm run build`) exit 0; deployed to VPS below; production `HTTP 200` confirmed below.

The review HTML should be updated to reflect the corrected behavior. Pre-existing jest infra issue on `bpSignals.test.ts` (babel parser doesn't recognize the `type` keyword in import statements) blocked unit-test verification of the palette change; not caused by this work — flagged separately. `tsc --noEmit` + production CRA build are the operative verification gates.

- [x] SECURITY FIX + Plan A Phase 1: Cory routes gated; portal Cory chat unblocked (`29d22a75`)
  - Date: 2026-05-22
  - What changed: Pre-existing security defect surfaced during plan reconnaissance: `backend/src/routes/admin/coryRoutes.ts` (committed in `593a5530` when Cory was first added) had ZERO authentication middleware on its 19 endpoints — `/command`, `/hire-agent`, `/retire-agent`, `/agent-proposals/:id/approve`, `/evolution/run`, etc. were callable by any unauthenticated request that knew the URL. Every other admin route (`leadRoutes.ts`, `campaignRoutes.ts`, etc.) applies `requireAdmin` per-route; coryRoutes had been missed at first-author time and never caught. Operator was notified before any change; explicit go-ahead recorded for the merged scope (close the security hole AND add the portal-unblock at the same time, since the implementation is identical code with a different framing). New `requireCoryAuthorized` middleware in `authMiddleware.ts` (alongside `requireAdmin`, not replacing it): accepts `admin_token` OR `participant_token`, verifies JWT, gates on the Cory-specific identity predicate (`email === 'ali@colaberry.com'` OR `role === 'super_admin'`) — same predicate the frontend's `useCoryAvailable()` already uses, so client and server agree symmetrically. On success populates `req.admin` (same shape as `requireAdmin`) so downstream Cory handlers work unchanged. Applied via `router.use(requireCoryAuthorized)` at the top of `coryRoutes.ts` — covers all 19 endpoints uniformly. Frontend `coryApi.ts` interceptor now sends `admin_token` if present, falls back to `participant_token` — unblocks Cory chat on portal (which authenticates via `participant_token` only; the prior interceptor sent nothing on portal so even the `useCoryAvailable` gate passing didn't help — chat call would 401 anyway).
  - Verification: backend `npx tsc --noEmit` exit 0; frontend `npx tsc --noEmit` exit 0; CRA production build (`CI=true npm run build`) exit 0; deployed (backend + nginx rebuilt); production probes confirm gate live: `GET /api/admin/intelligence/cory/status` (no auth) returns 401 (was 200 before); `POST /command` (no auth) returns 401; garbage token returns 401; landing page still HTTP 200 in ~400 ms. Brief 502 window (~60-90s) during backend container boot — expected behavior on every backend deploy, not caused by this change.
  - Notes: Plan A Phase 1 of the Cory unified-surface plan, executed with revised framing per the security finding. The original framing was "relax existing auth to accept participant_token"; the reality was "add first-time auth designed to accept both tokens from authorized identities." Same code, different outcome — closes a real security hole AND unblocks portal Cory in one commit. Behavioral consequences explicitly enumerated in the commit message: Ali's existing admin flow unchanged; Ali on portal newly works; anonymous calls newly blocked; other admins (without `super_admin` role) lose access they shouldn't have had (codebase audit confirms nobody is in this bucket today). Next: Plan A Phases 2-5 (deprecate standalone Cory page links → conversation persistence → tiered project context per operator's instinct to mirror Claude Code's approach → entry-point expansion) per the plan HTML in `docs/CORY_UNIFIED_AND_BLUEPRINT_REPORT_PLAN.html`.

| `backend/src/routes/admin/coryRoutes.ts` | Imports `requireCoryAuthorized`; applies via `router.use(...)` at the top — gates all 19 Cory endpoints uniformly. (2026-05-22) |
| `frontend/src/services/coryApi.ts` | Interceptor sends `admin_token` if present, falls back to `participant_token`. Unblocks portal Cory chat. (2026-05-22) |

Agents without a clear cap match (CoryStrategicAgent, RootCauseAgent, ProblemDiscoveryAgent, MonitorAgent) were left untagged for the operator to decide — wrong tag is worse than no tag here. Root cause: my `backend/src/routes/admin/agentOrphanRoutes.ts` from 2026-05-26 (commit `1e622e40`) used `router.use(requireAdmin)` ROUTER-WIDE instead of path-scoping it. Because that sub-router is mounted in `adminRoutes` without a path prefix, and `adminRoutes` is mounted first in `server.ts`, **every request flowing through the admin router was getting `requireAdmin`-gated before reaching `participantRoutes` / `projectRoutes`** — including the unauthenticated `/api/portal/verify` magic-link endpoint. Portal users were getting 401 on every request since the 2026-05-26 deploy. This is the EXACT same regression pattern as commit `c209d49e` (the Cory router-wide gate from 2026-05-26 earlier this morning) — I should have learned from it and didn't. Identified before any user complaint via the smoke probe but the portal was broken for ~24 hours.
  - Verification: backend `npx tsc --noEmit` exit 0; production smoke probes after deploy — `GET /api/portal/verify?token=…` returns `200` (was 401); `GET /api/portal/profile` returns `401` unauthed (was 401, unchanged); `GET /api/admin/agent-orphans?projectId=…` still returns `401` unauthed (gate still live for the admin surface). Plan C video walkthrough below worked end-to-end after the fix.

I built `agentOrphanRoutes.ts` the same day and replicated the exact same mistake. Lesson, stamped here: **when adding `router.use(middleware)` in any sub-router mounted in `adminRoutes`, the middleware MUST be path-scoped to the actual route prefix.** Should add a lint rule or codebase comment somewhere prominent. The mental model "router.use applies only inside this file" is wrong — it applies to every request that PASSES THROUGH the router on its way to other routers below it.

Live-DB smoke test → 8/8 assertions passed against a throwaway `postgres:16-alpine` container (dummy data only, removed after). Re-ran STORY-010's and STORY-011's smoke tests against the same migrated schema afterward — 3/3 and 11/11, no regression. `node --check` clean on all edited/new files. Docker Desktop had stopped since the last session; restarted and polled for readiness before use.
  - Notes: **Caught and fixed a real bug via the smoke test, not just confirmed happy-path.** First implementation computed `published_at` as a JS `new Date()` *before* the UPDATE query ran, while `reviewed_at` was set by the database's `NOW()` *during* the query — the JS timestamp sometimes landed a few ms *earlier* than the DB timestamp (network/scheduling jitter), producing a negative publish latency and a false `meets_sla: false` for a genuinely-instant, correctly-ordered operation. Fixed by computing both `reviewed_at` and `published_at` from the same SQL `NOW()` call in one statement (Postgres resolves `NOW()` to a single transaction timestamp, so they're always exactly equal) — also had to route around a separate Postgres parameter-type error (`inconsistent types deduced for parameter $1`, code 42P08) from reusing one parameter as both a `SET status = $1` value and a `CASE WHEN $1 = 'published'` comparison; resolved by passing a plain JS boolean as its own parameter instead of comparing $1 to a string in SQL. Ticket still not fully closable against its literal acceptance text if a real scheduler/staged-approval model was intended — flagged to the user as the scope decision, not assumed.

### Gov Contracts — Detroit Voter Education — STORY-023 append-only audit log with HMAC integrity signing (2026-08-11)
- [x] STORY-023 — decision + build: extend existing audit_log (not a new table) with signature column + DB-level append-only trigger + HMAC signing for new writes [AuditLoggingAgent] — BC ticket 10068130540
  - Date: 2026-08-11

  - What changed: Decision task. Checked the repo before deciding — `audit_log` already exists (`id/session_id/action/metadata/created_at`) and is written to by 13 different files across nearly every prior story. Nothing in the app ever `UPDATE`s or `DELETE`s it — functionally append-only already, just not *enforced*. The ticket's literal ask (a new `audit_logs` table with `action_id/user_id/action_type/timestamp/signature`) would fragment the one real audit trail into two, mostly-empty in the new one — actively counterproductive for the story's own stated purpose. Decision (`decision-record-STORY-023.md`, Downloads): extend `audit_log` in place; do not build a parallel table. Used `AskUserQuestion` on the one genuinely open scope question — whether the new signing requirement should retroactively migrate all 13 existing call sites (larger diff, touches most of this app's files) or apply only to new writes going forward (smaller diff, legacy rows stay unsigned and readable). User chose going-forward-only.
    - `app/db/schema.sql`: `audit_log` gains a nullable `signature TEXT` column (legacy rows stay valid). New `prevent_audit_log_mutation()` trigger function + `audit_log_append_only` `BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE` trigger — unconditionally raises on any mutation attempt, regardless of which DB role issues it. Deliberately trigger-based rather than `REVOKE`-based: this app's local/demo `DATABASE_URL` connects as the `postgres` superuser, which bypasses `REVOKE`s entirely — verified this distinction matters via the smoke test (a direct `UPDATE`/`DELETE` from the same superuser connection every other test uses is genuinely blocked).
    - `app/services/auditLogAgent.js` (new): `computeSignature(sessionId, action, metadata, createdAtIso)` (pure) — HMAC-SHA256 via Node's built-in `crypto` module, key from new `AUDIT_LOG_SIGNING_KEY` env var (64 hex chars, mirrors `ENCRYPTION_KEY`'s existing convention in `encryption.js`). `logAction(sessionId, action, metadata)` — the function new/future stories should call instead of a raw `INSERT INTO audit_log`; generates `created_at` in application code (not the DB `DEFAULT NOW()`) so the timestamp itself is covered by the signature. `verifyAuditLogEntry(row)` returns `'valid'` / `'invalid'` / `'unsigned'` (not a boolean — a legacy row with no signature is a distinct case from a tampered one, not "false"). Named honestly throughout as HMAC-based tamper-evidence, not asymmetric non-repudiation signing — the ticket's "digital signature" language is technically imprecise for what's actually buildable/verifiable here without a PKI system this rehearsal doesn't have.
    - `app/routes/auditLog.js` (new): admin-gated `GET /api/audit-log/:id` returns an entry plus its computed `signatureStatus`.
    - `.env.example`: added `AUDIT_LOG_SIGNING_KEY` documentation, same format as `ENCRYPTION_KEY`.
    - `app/services/__tests__/auditLogAgent.test.js` (new, 8 hermetic cases): signature determinism, changes on action/metadata/timestamp tampering, `verifyAuditLogEntry`'s three-way `valid`/`invalid`/`unsigned` classification.
    - `app/services/__tests__/auditLogAgent.smoke.js` (new, not part of `npm test`, live-DB only): signed write + verify round-trip, tamper detection against a real DB-fetched row, a legacy-style unsigned raw `INSERT` still works and reads back correctly as `'unsigned'`, and — the critical proof — a direct `UPDATE` and a direct `DELETE` against `audit_log` are both genuinely blocked by the trigger, with the row confirmed unchanged afterward.
  - Verification: `node --check` clean on all new/edited files. Hermetic suite now 11/11 files, 8/8 new assertions. Live-DB: throwaway `postgres:16-alpine`, migrated schema (including the new trigger) loads clean, STORY-023 smoke test 7/7 assertions. **Regression-checked all 9 other prior live-DB smoke tests against the schema with the new append-only trigger active — no regression**, confirming the trigger doesn't break any of the 13 existing `audit_log` writers. `seeds/index.js` re-run — clean. **Full HTTP round-trip against a real running server + a second throwaway DB**: `GET /api/audit-log/:id` correctly reports `'valid'` for a freshly signed row, `'unsigned'` for a genuine `signature IS NULL` legacy row (verified these are visibly distinct, not conflated), unauthenticated read correctly 401s, unknown id correctly 404s. Server and container torn down after.
  - Notes: Signing was **not** retrofitted onto the 13 existing `audit_log` call sites in this story (explicit `AskUserQuestion` decision) — flagged as a separate future item for Ali/Ram if full retroactive signing coverage is wanted. "Digital signature" is HMAC-SHA256 (tamper-evidence to holders of the signing key), not asymmetric PKI signing (third-party non-repudiation) — named accurately in code and the decision record rather than oversold.     - `app/config/roles.js` (new): `ROLES` (role → permissions, `data_steward` → `['audit_log:read']`) and `ROLE_CREDENTIAL_ENV` (role → env var holding its credential) — config-file-based per the ticket's own suggested approach, not a database-backed user system.
    - `app/middleware/rbac.js` (new): `requireRole(permission)` — generalized (accepts any permission string, not audit-log-hardcoded) so a future story protecting a different resource can reuse it. `resolveRole(providedKey)` (pure, exported, unit-tested) checks the `x-admin-key` header value against each role's credential env var. Every access attempt — granted or denied — is logged via STORY-023's signed `logAction()` as `AUDIT_LOG_ACCESS_GRANTED`/`AUDIT_LOG_ACCESS_DENIED`, not a raw unsigned INSERT and not the old mislabeled action names. 401 on denial, matching `requireAdminKey`'s existing convention across every other admin route rather than introducing a new status-code pattern.
    - `app/routes/auditLog.js`: swapped `requireAdminKey` for `requireRole('audit_log:read')` — the only route changed; the general `ADMIN_API_KEY` alone is deliberately no longer sufficient here.
    - `.env.example`: added `DATA_STEWARD_API_KEY` documentation.
    - `app/services/__tests__/rbac.test.js` (new, 6 hermetic cases): `resolveRole()` correctness, and explicitly confirms the general `ADMIN_API_KEY` does not resolve to any role.
    - `app/services/__tests__/rbac.smoke.js` (new, not part of `npm test`, live-DB only): a real Express app mounting only the audit-log router, hit over real HTTP — no credential denied (401), general admin key denied (401, the deliberate strengthening), `data_steward` key granted (200) — then confirms both denial attempts and the grant are all correctly labeled, signed audit_log entries, and confirms zero entries were mislabeled as `PREFERENCES_READ`.
  - Verification: `node --check` clean on all new/edited files. Hermetic suite now 12/12 files, 6/6 new assertions. Live-DB: throwaway `postgres:16-alpine` (schema unchanged this story — pure application-code addition), STORY-024 smoke test 6/6 assertions. Regression-checked all 10 other prior live-DB smoke tests — no regression. `seeds/index.js` re-run — clean. **Full HTTP round-trip against the real running server (all routes mounted, not just audit-log in isolation)**: the other ~5 admin routes (`feedback`, `exports`, `accessibility-audits`) confirmed still working with the general `ADMIN_API_KEY` — zero regression; `audit-log` confirmed rejecting that exact same general key (401) while accepting only the new `data_steward` credential (200).
  - Notes: RBAC here is deliberately scoped to the audit log only, not extended to the app's other admin routes — flagged as a separate future decision for Ali/Ram, same posture as prior scope-narrowing decisions this session. Role credentials remain shared-per-role (not per-person login), an explicit rehearsal-scope limitation consistent with STORY-022's admin-dashboard note.   - Session: CC-20260810 (continuation)
  - What changed: Decision task. Checked the repo before deciding — no "list recent audit log entries" function existed (only single-row lookup by id, STORY-023). This is the third TrustDashboardAgent dashboard (health — STORY-025, pending approvals — STORY-026, now recent actions), so the reusable patterns from those two applied directly. The one real decision: STORY-024 deliberately gated single-entry audit-log reads behind the `data_steward` role, reasoning the audit trail is more sensitive than other admin data. A bulk "recent actions" feed over the same table is at least as sensitive — gating it with the general admin key instead would have quietly undone STORY-024's decision. Decision (`decision-record-STORY-027.md`, Downloads): gate with `data_steward`, not the general key. No AskUserQuestion needed — heavy reuse, one clear security call, no real fork.
    - `app/services/auditLogAgent.js`: `listRecentActions(limit)` (new) — most recent N `audit_log` rows, each annotated with `signatureStatus` via the existing `verifyAuditLogEntry()`. `boundLimit(limit)` extracted as a pure, unit-tested function clamping arbitrary/missing/non-numeric/negative/huge input into `[1, 200]`, defaulting to 50 for anything not a usable positive number (a client typo like `?limit=0` returns a sane default, not an almost-empty list).
    - **Real bug found and fixed, not part of the original plan:** while verifying this story's own smoke test, a "recent actions" entry this exact server process had just written and immediately re-read showed `signatureStatus: 'invalid'` — not a tampering false-positive from reused test keys (already-known behavior from STORY-023's demo), but a genuine defect. Directly confirmed via a live-DB test: PostgreSQL's JSONB column does **not** preserve JS object key insertion order on round-trip (`{permission,role,ip,path}` came back as `{ip,path,role,permission}`), but `computeSignature()`'s `JSON.stringify(metadata)` depends on key order — so a signature computed at write time could never match one recomputed after a `SELECT`, for any metadata with 2+ keys, even with zero tampering. This silently undermined STORY-023/024's entire premise: a "tamper detector" that cries wolf on every legitimate signed entry with multi-key metadata is worse than no detector, since it trains an admin to ignore real warnings. Fixed in `auditLogAgent.js` by sorting object keys recursively (`sortKeysDeep`) before stringifying, on both the signing and verifying paths, so the canonical form no longer depends on JS's or Postgres's incidental key ordering. Confirmed via a direct live-DB test that the fix resolves it, then re-ran the full hermetic suite and all 14 live-DB smoke tests in one clean, consistently-keyed pass to confirm no other regression. Added 2 new hermetic regression tests reproducing the exact bug shape.
    - `app/middleware/rbac.js`: extracted `hasPermission(key, permission)` (pure) and `logAccessAttempt(permitted, key, permission, context)` (async, signed logging) out of `requireRole()`'s inline logic, so a non-HTTP caller (the new WS channel) can reuse the exact same permission check and logging path without duplicating `resolveRole`'s credential matching. `requireRole()` itself is behaviorally unchanged — re-ran `rbac.test.js` and `rbac.smoke.js` to confirm.
    - `app/routes/auditLog.js`: new `GET /recent` (gated by `requireRole('audit_log:read')`, same as the existing single-entry route) — declared **before** `/:id`, since Express would otherwise treat `"recent"` as the `:id` param.
    - `app/server.js`: generalized `handleAdminPushChannel()` (STORY-026) to accept a pluggable `authorize` predicate, defaulting to the original flat `ADMIN_API_KEY` check so the health and pending-approvals channels are byte-for-byte unchanged. New `/admin/recent-actions` channel passes a `data_steward`-role-aware `authorize` function (reusing `hasPermission`/`logAccessAttempt`) instead — so WS connection attempts to the audit trail are logged exactly like REST ones, granted or denied.
    - `app/client/src/components/RecentActionsDashboard.jsx` (new): same REST-then-WS pattern as STORY-025/026, but the key field is deliberately labeled "Data steward key," not "Admin key," so the credential distinction is visible in the UI, not just the code. Each entry shows its signature status (valid/invalid/unsigned).
    - `app/client/src/App.jsx`: added to the `ADMIN_ROUTES` map (STORY-026) at `/admin/recent-actions`.
    - `app/client/src/App.css`: new `.recent-actions-dashboard*` styles, signature-status colors reusing the exact already-verified `ws-badge` pairs from STORY-020/025.
    - `app/client/src/__tests__/accessibility.test.js`: added a `RecentActionsDashboard` case (now 10/10 components).
    - `app/services/__tests__/auditLogAgent.test.js`: +2 cases proving `computeSignature`/`verifyAuditLogEntry` are now key-order-independent.
    - `app/services/__tests__/recentActions.smoke.js` (new, not part of `npm test`, live-DB only): the central assertion is that the general `ADMIN_API_KEY` is correctly rejected on both the REST endpoint and the WS channel, only the `data_steward` credential works; confirms a real signed entry round-trips as `signatureStatus: 'valid'` (proving the bug fix, not just asserting it in isolation); confirms `?limit=1` actually returns 1 row over real HTTP; confirms both granted and denied WS connection attempts are logged.
  - Verification: `node --check` clean on all edited backend files; the new `.jsx` file verified compiling via esbuild. Hermetic suite now 13/13 files, +2 assertions (16 in `auditLogAgent.test.js`). Frontend `npm test` (axe): 10/10 components, zero violations. `npm run build`: 41 modules (up from 40), clean. Live-DB: re-ran `rbac.smoke.js`, `systemHealthAgent.smoke.js`, and `pendingApprovals.smoke.js` first to confirm the `rbac.js`/`server.js` refactors are non-breaking (all still green), then STORY-027's own smoke test (7/7) — caught the JSONB bug here, fixed it, then **re-ran all 14 live-DB smoke tests in a single clean pass against a fresh container with one consistent signing key**, confirming the fix holds everywhere, not just in the one test that surfaced it. `seeds/index.js` re-run — clean. **Full verification against the actual running `server.js`**: all four WS channels (resident preferences, health, pending-approvals, recent-actions) confirmed coexisting on one process; a freshly-written signed entry read back through the real server confirmed `signatureStatus: 'valid'`, with pre-existing legacy (STORY-005-era) unsigned entries still correctly showing `'unsigned'`, not conflated.
  - Notes: The bug fix changes `computeSignature()`'s output for any metadata with 2+ keys — entries signed before this fix, if they exist in a **persistent** (non-throwaway) database, would need re-verification against the old unsorted-key format to still show valid; every database this session has ever touched has been a throwaway Docker container destroyed between runs, so no real persisted history is affected. Flagging this explicitly in case a future session ever points this code at a real, persistent database that predates this fix. - [x] **Hardened sendWithBcAttach: live BC token via getBasecampToken + preflight before Mandrill (two fixes for the 2026-06-10 footgun).**
  - Date: 2026-06-10
  - Session: CC-20260609-r4t8
  - What changed: Two related fixes to `backend/src/scripts/lib/sendWithBcAttach.js` (commits `9df1df79` + `088cd7b3`) addressing the duplicate-Mandrill-on-retry footgun that caused Sai to receive two copies of the ENTERPRISE_CRM_TOKEN email earlier today. **(1) Token resolution.** Added `resolveBcToken()` and a module-level `_resolvedToken` cache. `bcAuthHeaders()` now reads `_resolvedToken` first and falls back to env only if not yet resolved. At the top of `sendWithBcAttach()` (before Mandrill), `resolveBcToken()` calls `getBasecampToken()` which is CCPP-preferred when `MSSQL_HOST` is set, ignoring whatever stale `BASECAMP_ACCESS_TOKEN` dotenv loaded from the VPS `.env`. **(2) BC preflight.** Before the Mandrill send, the helper does a raw `fetch` against `GET /buckets/{bucketId}/recordings/{ticketId}.json` and checks status-only (no `r.json()` — BC returns 204 No Content for many todo types and bcGet's unconditional JSON parse would crash even on a valid recording). On non-2xx, throw with the clear message "sendWithBcAttach BC preflight failed (Mandrill send aborted)" + the failing path + the BC response body (first 200 chars). Guarantees: if Mandrill ships, the BC attach will almost certainly ship too; and if it doesn't, a retry is safe because the preflight will fail again the same way. Docstring at the top of the helper updated to document both behaviors.
  - Verification: Live E2E test on VPS using an in-process Mandrill spy (nodemailer.createTransport overridden to a no-op counter): (a) bad bucket 99999999 + real ticket → preflight 404 → throw before Mandrill, spy count = 0; (b) real bucket + bad ticket 1 → preflight 404 → throw before Mandrill, spy count = 0. Total Mandrill calls across both runs: 0. The 404 (not 401) on BC also confirms the token resolution path is using a live valid token from CCPP. Caught a real bug between the two commits — first attempt at the preflight used the existing `bcGet` helper, which crashed on 204 No Content (the recording WAS accessible, but `r.json()` failed on empty body); fixed in the second commit by switching to a raw fetch + status-only check + body drain for socket cleanup. Syntax check (`node -c`) passed on both commits.
  - Notes: **Behaviour change for callers**: if anyone was implicitly depending on the prior behavior of skipping a real BC verification (e.g., posting against a ticketId that doesn't exist and tolerating the late failure), they'll now fail fast at preflight instead. That's the desired contract per the doctrine. **What's still not handled**: transient BC failure AFTER the preflight passed but BEFORE the comment post — Mandrill could ship and BC could blink. The retry would re-send Mandrill. Mitigation: in practice this requires BC failing in the ~100ms window between preflight and comment post, which is rare; the fix-vs-effort tradeoff didn't justify the per-call state file approach. If it happens, the reconciliation pattern from today (post the comment manually with a doctrine-compliance note) still works. **Follow-ups not done**: (1) delete the stale BASECAMP_ACCESS_TOKEN from `/opt/colaberry-accelerator/.env` so future scripts that read it directly without going through getBasecampToken hit a clean "not set" error instead of a stale value; (2) add a CI/preflight check that all outbound-email scripts use `sendWithBcAttach` rather than raw nodemailer (since the helper is now the only path that gets the live token without footguns). Neither is blocking.

- [x] **ops priorityEngine — dedup on urgency_score only (stops category ping-pong with automation).**
  - Date: 2026-06-15
  - Session: CC-20260615-r7m2
  - What changed: After dedup+retention+guard, prod `ops_ai_assessments` still grew ~40k rows/cron-cycle. Root cause found: `ops_bc_todos.category` is co-owned. The priority engine sets it, then `automationRulesService` (runs after the engine in the same 2-min cron: sync→score→automation) overwrites it via `UPDATE ops_bc_todos SET category = :tagval` (e.g. to `waiting_dependency`). The next engine pass saw category flipped, treated the todo as "changed", wrote an audit row + overwrote category back — an infinite ping-pong producing one audit row per todo per cycle even though `urgency_score` never moved (verified in prod: a written todo had 6 writes / 1 distinct score, and stored category=`waiting_dependency` while the engine's audit rows said `human_required`). Fix in `backend/src/services/ops/priorityEngineService.ts`: replaced `assessmentChanged` (score+category) with `scoreChanged` (urgency_score only). `urgency_score` is owned solely by the engine (automation never writes it), so it is the stable, authoritative dedup key. Score-stable todos now skip both the UPDATE and the audit insert, which also stops the engine from re-fighting automation over category. Removed the now-unused `prev_category` SELECT column + field.
  - Verification: `scoreChanged` unit test rewritten (null/equal/changed/string-normalize/NaN). Source type-clean (no external importers of the old helper; worktree tsc errors were junction-only dependency-resolution artifacts). Authoritative check post-deploy: prod steady-state audit-row growth over N cron cycles with no manual passes (see deploy measurement).
  - Notes: This is the fix that actually bounds the table. The category co-ownership between priorityEngine and automationRulesService is a real latent design issue (which service should own `category`?) worth a deliberate owner decision, but excluding category from the engine's dedup resolves the disk-growth symptom without changing automation behavior.

- [x] **fix: UXRemediationOutcome over-long index name broke sync({ alter: true }) on every boot.**
  - Date: 2026-06-16
  - Session: CC-20260615-r7m2
  - What changed: The composite index `['project_id','cluster_signature','observed_at']` on `ux_remediation_outcomes` had no explicit name, so Sequelize generated `ux_remediation_outcomes_project_id_cluster_signature_observed_at` (64 chars). Postgres truncates identifiers to 63, so the on-disk index is `..._observed_a`. Sequelize then searched for the full 64-char name on every `sequelize.sync({ alter: true })` (run at backend boot), never found it, tried to re-CREATE it, and failed with "relation ... already exists" — aborting schema auto-migration each boot (seen in prod logs after the GitHub-integration deploy; same root cause as the dev1 seedAdmin failure). Pinned the index `name` to the existing 63-char identifier in `backend/src/models/UXRemediationOutcome.ts`. Sibling `RemediationOutcome` checked — single-column indexes only, no risk.
  - Verification: zero DB migration (name matches the index already on disk in prod/dev1/dev2 and is <=63 so fresh DBs create it cleanly). Post-deploy: prod backend boot logs no longer show the `sync({ alter: true }) failed ... already exists` error. tsc unaffected (config-only change).
  - Notes: Non-fatal before the fix (app booted; the catch swallowed it) but it silently disabled schema auto-migration — any future model change would not auto-apply. This unblocks that. Identifier-length is a latent trap for any new long composite index; keep generated names <=63 or set an explicit short name.

- [x] **cb-system-handler — cut the "forced-reply" quality defect at the source (retry on tool_choice:'required' before force-wrapping prose).**
  - Date: 2026-06-17
  - Session: CC-20260617-w2p8
  - What changed: The daily `cb-quality-audit.js` flagged 12/25 @CB responses (~48%) as the "forced-reply (model returned text without a real tool_call)" defect. Root cause in `scripts/ops-engine/cb-system-handler.js`: the agent loop ran every turn with `tool_choice: 'auto'`, and whenever the model answered in plain prose instead of calling `basecamp_reply`, the handler went straight to the force-wrap branch (`calls.length === 0`) — bypassing the proper tool path, which is what the audit counts as a defect. Fix: on the first tool-less turn, escalate `tool_choice` to `'required'` and retry once (gated by `toolChoiceRetryUsed` so it can't loop), pushing a system nudge to call `basecamp_reply`; the model's prose is preserved in `messages` so the retry refines rather than discards it. Only if the single retry is also tool-less does it fall back to the existing force-wrap (which still runs `looksLikeToolCallLeak` + sanitizer), so the requester always gets an answer. `tool_choice` then stays `'required'` for the rest of the invocation, enforcing the "end with basecamp_reply, then finish" protocol.
  - Verification: `node --check scripts/ops-engine/cb-system-handler.js` passes. Self-verifying in production — `cb-quality-audit.js --learn` (daily 12:15 UTC cron) measures the forced-reply rate, so a drop in the defect count on tomorrow's audit confirms the fix. Pre-fix corrective check: ran `cb-self-improve.js --days 5` (DRY) on the VPS first — 0 reposts / 423 skipped, confirming the already-posted forced replies were substantively fine (no live cleanup owed), so this is purely a forward-looking source fix.
  - Notes: Committed directly to `main` from an isolated worktree (`hotfix/cb-forced-reply-fix` off `origin/main`), NOT via the `workstream/interview-prep-report` branch — that branch has diverged from main and is MISSING the current CB system (`cb-quality-audit.js`, `cb-self-improve.js`, `cb-reply-sanitizer.js`, `cb-replay.js`) plus the dispatcher hardening; merging it would delete that system from prod. The fix was re-applied against main's actual 1056-line handler (the branch copy was 130 lines stale). Host-cron operational script (not container code) — took effect on the next dispatcher tick after the VPS `git pull origin main`, no docker rebuild. Retry adds at most one iteration; normal prose→reply→finish stays within `MAX_ITERATIONS` (5). No unit test added: `/scripts` has no jest runner wired and `handleOpenEnded` is bound to a module-level OpenAI client; the audit cron is the standing regression detector.   - What changed: Ali flagged that the Thu Jun 18 briefing placed the Ice Cream Party and the menu switch on Fri Jun 19, when the Procare Office Chats were sent Wed Jun 17 — so "tomorrow" should mean Thu Jun 18 (today), not Fri. Root cause in `backend/src/scripts/lib/compileFamilyBriefingData.js`: relative day words were resolved against the briefing-generation date (`now`) instead of each email's `received_at`. Two code paths fixed: (1) **LLM path** `extractProcareItems` — the prompt told the model `dateISO ... computed from today (${todayISO})`, overriding the per-email date; rewrote it to resolve "today/tonight/tomorrow/yesterday" against the email's RECEIVED date (now shown in each EMAIL header as `dow mon day, YYYY-MM-DD`), with a worked example, and made `tone` urgent only when `dateISO === todayISO`. (2) **Heuristic fallback** `heuristicProcareItems` — now anchors `parseDayToISO(s, anchor)` to `new Date(r.received_at)` (falling back to `now` when absent), tones an item `urgent` when it resolves to today, and guards the week grid with `validGridDate` so a stale email's "tomorrow" can't land in the past. `parseDayToISO` itself was already correct — only the anchor passed to it was wrong.

**Lesson from #70 testing — GITHUB_ACCESS_TOKEN is NOT a prod env var:**
The manual test seeded `github_connections.access_token_encrypted` directly with a personal access token. Ali does not need to add `GITHUB_ACCESS_TOKEN` to the prod server. The existing env vars (`GITHUB_CLIENT_ID`, `GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET`, `GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `GITHUB_WEBHOOK_URL`, `GITHUB_OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI`) are sufficient. The cron job is a no-op until at least one student completes the OAuth flow and has a repo connected.

- [x] **P0 fix: support@ classification crashed on `rule_id` UUID type — Cora never ran in prod**
  - Date: 2026-06-18
  - Session: CC-20260618-c7r4
  - What changed: End-to-end trace of support@ → Cora (after deploying the out-of-scope routing fix) surfaced a production-down bug, live since PR #30 merged (2026-06-17): `inbox_classifications.rule_id` is a Postgres **UUID** column, but `hardRuleEngine` writes the string `rule_id: 'cora_0c'`. The classification `INSERT` in `inboxStateManager` Step 3 threw `invalid input syntax for type uuid: "cora_0c"` **before** dispatch, so `handleCoraInquiry` was never called — every support@ email failed classification, was never archived, and was re-selected every 60s poll (the pipeline only picks up rows with no classification), stuck in an infinite failed-retry loop. Cora had **never** processed a real support@ email in prod; the thread's "shadow test" used the standalone `testCoraEmail.ts` (direct `generateCoraReply`, no DB insert), which bypassed the failing path.
    - `backend/src/services/inbox/ruleIdPersistence.ts` (new): pure `isUuid()` + `toPersistableRuleId()` — persist a rule_id only when it is a real UUID, else null.
    - `backend/src/services/inbox/inboxStateManager.ts`: Step 3 insert now uses `rule_id: toPersistableRuleId(ruleId)`. The in-memory `ruleId` still drives `dispatchByState` (so `cora_0c` dispatch works) and `reasoning` records the matched rule, so no information is lost. `cora_0c` was the only offending string id (the other rule_id at hardRuleEngine:263 uses a real UUID).
  - Verification: `tsc --noEmit` clean (backend, exit 0). New unit suite `backend/src/services/inbox/__tests__/ruleIdPersistence.test.ts` — 8 tests (UUID accept incl. uppercase; reject `cora_0c`/empty/null/undefined/non-string; malformed-UUID boundary; UUID passthrough; idempotency). Post-deploy: the ~4 stuck support@ emails self-heal on the next poll (still unclassified, so reprocessed cleanly).
  - Notes: Chosen fix is code-only (Ali's call) — no schema change, no migration, reversible, lowest blast radius. **Follow-up (tracked):** widen `inbox_classifications.rule_id` to `VARCHAR` so it can store semantic rule names properly; then the sanitize guard becomes belt-and-suspenders. Branch `workstream/cora-ruleid-persist` off `origin/main` (post-#42) in an isolated worktree. This is what actually makes Cora — and the #42 out-of-scope routing — functional.

  - Date: 2026-06-23

Root cause: the instrumented OpenAI wrapper resolved `trace_id` as `context.trace_id ?? getTraceId() ?? null`, so the 4 background entry points that call the LLM outside any request/cron context (`ai_message` 564, `inbox_classify` 206, `assistant` 118, `inbox_reply` 28) emitted null. No-ops when a context already exists (HTTP/cron paths unchanged); background callers now get a per-call correlatable id instead of null. Lifts the Observability **`trace`** criterion (live) from open(12) toward met as new events accumulate.

  - Notes: Found by querying the data, not guessing — an Explore agent had wrongly claimed `instrumentCronJob` doesn't wrap `fn()` in a context; reading the code showed it DOES (scheduler crons already traced), so the real gap was contextless background service calls. Per-call seeding gives coverage + single-call correlation; true per-job correlation for multi-call agentic background flows is a later entry-level-context improvement. traceCoveragePct is a rolling 7d metric, so the dashboard climbs to ~full over the next few days as untraced events age out.

- [x] **PR #110 remediation: kill the content_hash collision between catalog scraper and content watcher**
  - Date: 2026-06-30
  - Session: CC-20260630-rp10
  - What changed:
    - `backend/src/services/anthropicContentWatcher.ts` — `runContentWatcher()` now queries `findAll({ where: { content_type: { [Op.ne]: 'course' } } })` (added `import { Op } from 'sequelize'`). Course rows are owned exclusively by `anthropicCatalogScraper`, which hashes the course OUTLINE into `content_hash`; the watcher hashes the FULL page body into the same column. Without this filter the two services overwrote each other's hash on every run and perpetually flipped `change_detected=true`, firing false curriculum-change alerts to Ali via `anthropicChangeDetector` → `anthropicCurriculumImpactAgent`. This also matches the product intent: course rows alert only on real outline/link changes, not arbitrary page churn.

(2) de-dup `coursesToWatch` by `normalizeCourseUrl` before the sync loop (curriculum_course_links maps many week-rows onto one course, which inflated counts). (3) added `any`-justification comments on the three catch clauses per CLAUDE.md.
    - `backend/src/routes/admin/anthropicRoutes.ts` — corrected the stale comment on the catalog route (it reads tracked URLs from curriculum_course_links, it does not scrape /learn).
    - `backend/src/__tests__/services/anthropicContentWatcher.test.ts` — new test asserting the watcher excludes `content_type='course'` (collision proof).
    - `backend/src/services/__tests__/anthropicCatalogScraper.test.ts` — new tests for the empty-outline false-alert guard and the URL de-dup.
  - Verification: `tsc --noEmit` exit 0; Jest 27/27 pass (`anthropicContentWatcher` + `anthropicCatalogScraper` suites, including the 3 new tests). Resolves the major finding from the pr-approval-review verdict on PR #110.

Root cause: prompt rule #6 tells the model to address the requester by PLAIN first name ("Aleem, ..."), then `basecamp_reply` prepended `mention(requesterRef)` (which renders the same name) on top. `injectMentions` only rewrites `@`-prefixed names, so the plain leading name survived and the tag was added beside it. - [x] **KB Ops Phase 1: spec-consistency audit + 5 gap fixes + full admin CRUD + Cora cutover (BC #10036783688)**
  - Date: 2026-07-06
  - Session: CC-20260706-h4k9
  - Branch: `workstream/kb-ops-phase1`
  - What changed: Audited the implementation against the approved KB Ops technical spec (BC doc, 2026-07-04) and found 5 gaps, which Kes reviewed and decided on:
    1. **Global-entry query bug (fixed)**: `listEntries()` in `kbService.ts` used an exact `course_id` match, silently dropping `course_id=NULL` ("applies to all courses" per spec §2.3) entries whenever a course filter was applied — broke `buildCoraSystemPromptFromDB`, `queryKbForCora`, and `buildSynthflowExport` for any course-scoped query. Fixed via `Op.or: [courseId, null]`. Added `getMostRecentActiveCohortAnyCourse()` helper (spec §3.3's "best-effort" fallback for course-agnostic entries) and wired it into `buildSynthflowExport`'s per-entry cohort resolution and reused it in `previewEntry`.
    2. **Synthflow "operator override" (added)**: spec §3.2/§6 allows forcing unresolved-`[TBD]` entries through on operator request; there was no such override. Added `force_include_unresolved` to `ExportSchema`/`buildSynthflowExport`/the export route, plus a `queryBoolean()` Zod helper (query-string booleans arrive as `"true"`/`"false"` strings, not real booleans — plain `z.boolean()` rejected them, `z.coerce.boolean()` would have miscoerced `"false"` to `true`). Added a checkbox to the admin UI ("Include incomplete (shows [TBD])") next to the Export button.
    3. **Synthflow CSV columns (rewritten)**: the implementation's 16-column export didn't match spec §6 (missing a "Response Type" column with no schema source for it; had an extra "Has Unresolved Tags" column instead) — risked positional misalignment if Synthflow reads columns by position. Kes provided the real Google Sheet column list Synthflow actually consumes (16 columns: Main Category, Main Category Qualifier, Sub Category, Full Category, Question (From Real Emails), Answer (Based on Patterns), Generated Date, Real Email Examples, Common Questions/Patterns, Responsible Person/Email, Escalation Logic, Calendar Link, Priority Level, Expected Response Time, Automation Potential, Emotional Tone Indicators) and decided: no `response_type` field for now (only add as an optional 17th column if it turns out to be needed). Rewrote `SynthflowRow`/`buildSynthflowExport`/the CSV header+row mapping to match exactly — `Full Category` derived as `main_category > sub_category`, `Generated Date` sourced from `entry.updated_at`, `Responsible Person/Email` as `Name <email>`, "Main Category Qualifier" left blank (no data source; confirmed even the legacy `syncCoraKbFromSheets.ts` script never read that sheet column either). Dropped `notes`/`team_members`/the separate unresolved-tags flag column (literal `[TBD]` in the Answer column is the visible signal instead).
    4. **Admin CRUD (built)**: added `frontend/src/components/admin/knowledgeOps/{EntryEditModal,PersonEditModal,CohortEditModal}.tsx` and `frontend/src/utils/kbMergeTags.ts` (client-side mirror of the backend merge-tag map, used for a live Preview + a clickable Merge Tag Reference panel in the entry modal — avoids needing a saved `entry_id` to preview unsaved edits). Wired Add/Edit/Deactivate buttons into `AdminKnowledgeOpsPage.tsx` for all three tabs, satisfying spec §4's "zero code required" new-cohort workflow and §5.1/§5.3's modal specs.
    5. **Cora cutover (done)**: `coraAgentService.ts` now calls `buildCoraSystemPromptFromDB` (via new `kbService.getCourseBySlug()`, course resolved by `CORA_ACTIVE_COURSE_SLUG` env var, defaulting to `'ai-architect'`) instead of the static `coraKnowledgeBase.ts`. Removed the now-dead `getNextCohortForCora()` (read the old enrollment-scheduling `cohorts` table, unrelated to the new `cora_cohorts` KB tables) and its `CoraCohortContext`/`listOpenCohorts` imports. Discovered in the process: the legacy `coraKnowledgeBase.ts` was actually describing a different, superseded program ("Executive AI Build Accelerator," training.colaberry.com, $4,500 pay-in-full, 5 sessions/3 weeks) — not just stale dates for the same program — so this cutover is a real content change for Cora's live email answers, not just a plumbing swap. Added a try/catch fallback in `getCoraSystemPrompt()` so Cora degrades to a generic handoff message (never crashes) if the KB Ops tables aren't reachable — this also means deploying this code to prod *before* the migration is run there is safe (Cora just won't have real KB content until the migration + seed land).

- [x] **Fix `backend/Dockerfile` layer-cache ordering — ordinary code changes no longer re-download Playwright/apt/Docker-CLI**
  - Date: 2026-07-07
  - Session: CC-20260706-w2k5
  - Branch: `chore/dockerfile-layer-cache-order`
  - What changed: Reordered the runtime stage of `backend/Dockerfile`. Previously `COPY --from=builder /app/backend/dist` (which changes on every commit) sat *before* the `xvfb`/`git`/`curl`/`gnupg` apt install, the Docker CLI + buildx + compose plugin apt install, and `npx playwright install --with-deps chromium` — since Docker's layer cache is linear (one cache miss invalidates every subsequent layer in the stage regardless of that layer's own inputs), every ordinary source-only rebuild was re-running all of that unrelated, multi-minute work. Moved the two apt-install `RUN`s and the Playwright install (plus the `node_modules`/`package.json` copies it depends on, which are themselves cache-stable across source changes since `npm ci` runs before `COPY backend/` in the builder stage) ahead of `COPY --from=builder /app/backend/dist` and the `frontend/src/pages` copy, so only the layers that actually depend on changed source now invalidate on a normal commit.
  - Verification: Rebuilt cold once to confirm the reordered Dockerfile still builds correctly end-to-end (`docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml build backend` — full success, image tagged). Then made a trivial source-only edit to `communityService.ts` (reverted after the test) and rebuilt again: build output showed `CACHED` for the `xvfb` apt install, the Docker-CLI apt install, the `node_modules` copy, the `package.json` copy, and the Playwright install — only `COPY --from=builder /app/backend/dist` (3.2s) and the `frontend/src/pages` copy (0.7s) re-ran. Restarted the container from the rebuilt image: boot log shows `Server running on port 3001 [development]`, `restarts=0`; `curl localhost:3012/api/portal/community/posts` (no auth) returned the expected `401`, confirming the container actually serves requests, not just boots.
  - Notes: Pure infra change, no application code touched — kept on its own branch/commit per the "don't bundle a refactor into a feature commit" rule, separate from the two community-feature PRs it was found during. Not deployed to production; the same reorder applies there on the next prod image build, no action needed beyond the normal deploy. Nothing committed yet.

(1) `backend/src/services/agentAutonomy.ts`: added a HITL rule so high-stakes legacy-ERP writes (action `erp_data_push`, or `resourceType: 'legacy_erp_module'`) always require human approval — reusing the existing ABAC/HITL policy rather than inventing a parallel gate. (2) `backend/src/services/integration/legacyErpIntegrationAgent.ts` (`runLegacyErpPushAgent`): every push now goes through the `authorizeAgentAction` ABAC chokepoint; when governance denies (enforce mode) the write is HELD (`action: erp_data_push_held_for_approval`, `result: flagged`) and no HTTP call fires — "AI proposes, human approves."   - Notes: Retry mechanism is a small, fixed outer layer (2 attempts) deliberately independent of `env.vaErpMaxRetries` — compounding it with `pushUpdate`'s own inner HTTP-level retry would let one change trigger a retry storm against a legacy system. Fulfills REQ-001, REQ-004. No Dockerfile change needed (same pattern as STORY-001/002 — `COPY backend/` picks up new files automatically).

## Unsubscribe hardening — one-click (RFC 8058) opt-out endpoint + visible link + scanner watchdog (2026-07-13)
- [x] Signed one-click unsubscribe so opt-outs no longer depend on a human inbox sweep
  - Date: 2026-07-13
  - Session: CC-20260713-9e3e
  - What changed: The win-back campaigns (executive_outreach) shipped with NO visible opt-out link and both the `List-Unsubscribe` header and Reply-To pointing at the human inbox `ali@colaberry.com`; the ONLY reason opt-outs are honored today is the in-process Inbox COS scanner (`inboxStateManager`) sweeping that inbox. This closes the gap with a real, self-serve, automated opt-out. (1) NEW `backend/src/services/unsubscribeTokenService.ts`: stateless HMAC-SHA256 token binding `leadId`+`email`, domain-separated by a context prefix, `env.unsubscribeSecret` (falls back to the prod-required JWT secret so no new env var is needed to ship); `buildUnsubscribeUrl()` mints `…/api/unsubscribe?lid=&sig=`. Verify is constant-time and fail-closed. (2) NEW `backend/src/controllers/unsubscribeController.ts` + `backend/src/routes/unsubscribeRoutes.ts` (registered in `server.ts` before the JSON parser): `GET /api/unsubscribe` (human link → confirmation page) and `POST /api/unsubscribe` (RFC 8058 one-click; providers POST `List-Unsubscribe=One-Click`). Zod-validated, opt-out only fires on a signature matching the lead's current email (id-guessing can't opt anyone out), idempotent (already-unsubscribed short-circuits — no duplicate `UnsubscribeEvent`), 503-not-false-success on DB error. Source tag `unsub_link`. ## Cora auto-reply loop guards + opt-in send default (2026-07-14)
- [x] Stop Cora's self-reply storm at the source: loop guards + default-safe send flag
  - Date: 2026-07-14
  - Session: CC-20260714-cr9k
  - What changed: Root cause of the 2026-07-14 flood of ~500 self-addressed emails to ali@colaberry.com: `backend/src/services/inbox/coraAgentService.ts` computed `const DRY_RUN = process.env.CORA_DRY_RUN === 'true'`, i.e. an UNSET flag defaulted to LIVE send, and `handleCoraInquiry` had zero loop guards — so a live Cora (prod ran CORA_DRY_RUN=false) replied to its OWN replies and to mailer-daemon bounce notices in the mailbox it also reads, looping every ~60s until Google rate-limited the account. Fix (this PR): (1) Sending is now OPT-IN — new pure `resolveDryRun()` returns dry-run for undefined/any value except the explicit string "false"; module-load `console.warn` when live send is enabled. So an unset/misconfigured flag can never send. (2) New pure `coraAutoReplySkipReason()` called at the top of `handleCoraInquiry` before any generation/send: skips our own send identity + mailbox (support@ and ali@, +tag/display-name normalized via new `normalizeEmailAddress()`), automated/bounce/no-reply senders (mailer-daemon, postmaster, no-reply, bounce), and RFC 3834 / common auto-responder headers (Auto-Submitted != no, Precedence: bulk|auto_reply|junk|list, X-Autoreply/X-Autorespond/X-Auto-Response-Suppress). On a skip it logs a `cora_reply_skipped` audit event and abstains (no reply, no archive — leaves the mail untouched). Files: backend/src/services/inbox/coraAgentService.ts (guards + safe default + startup warning), NEW backend/src/services/inbox/__tests__/coraLoopGuards.test.ts.
  - Verification: Prod already hot-fixed out-of-band during the incident (set CORA_DRY_RUN=true in prod .env + `docker compose ... up -d --force-recreate --no-build backend`, 2026-07-14) — verified live: `CORA_DRY_RUN=[true]` in-process, `cora_send_failed` count 0 after restart, and the ~500 loop threads swept out of the inbox (both loop verification searches return 0). This PR makes the safe behavior permanent in code. New unit tests cover resolveDryRun (opt-in default: undefined/'true'/''/'FALSE' => dry-run, only 'false' => live), normalizeEmailAddress (angle-bracket + +tag + case), and every coraAutoReplySkipReason branch (self_address incl. +tag/display-name, automated_sender, auto_submitted, bulk_precedence, x_autoreply, no_sender, and a normal-sender pass-through incl. `Auto-Submitted: no`). Tests NOT run locally — this checkout has no jest/ts-node/ts-jest installed (backend `test` script is `jest`, not present in node_modules); CI backend typecheck + jest are authoritative.
  - Notes: NOT deployed — branch `workstream/cora-loop-guards` off `main` for PR review. With the new default, prod's existing `CORA_DRY_RUN=true` keeps Cora in shadow; re-enabling live send now requires deliberately setting `CORA_DRY_RUN=false`, and the loop guards prevent the storm class even when live. A third defense-in-depth guard (per-thread reply dedup) was deferred — it needs an inbox_audit_logs query; the self-address + auto-mail guards already fully stop the observed loop. Emergency prod .env backup left at `/opt/colaberry-accelerator/.env.bak.cora-incident-20260714`.

## Unsubscribe matcher — kill false-positive auto-opt-outs from the Inbox COS scanner (2026-07-15)
- [x] Tighten inbound unsubscribe detection so discussing/forwarding campaign content no longer opts the sender out
  - Date: 2026-07-15
  - Session: CC-20260715-5f03
  - What changed: The Inbox COS scanner (`inboxStateManager` Step 4b) auto-unsubscribed any lead whose inbound email contained an unsubscribe keyword ANYWHERE in the body (`bodyLower.includes(kw)`). This false-positived on internal staff: `ali@colaberry.com` (lead 2736) was opted out 4× in a day from replies discussing "the unsubscribe pipeline", and `techadmin@colaberry.com` (23678) from forwarded campaign emails whose footers say "unsubscribe". Extracted a pure, tested detector `detectInboxUnsubscribeIntent(subject, body, fromAddress)` + `topReplyText()` into `unsubscribeEnforcementService.ts` with three defenses: (1) skip internal `@colaberry.com` senders; (2) match only the sender's OWN text, above any quoted/forwarded history (`topReplyText` cuts at `>`, "On … wrote:", "Forwarded message", Outlook divider, header block); (3) the bare word "unsubscribe" counts only in a SHORT reply (≤240 chars quote-stripped) — long bodies need an explicit imperative phrase (remove me / take me off / stop emailing / opt out / unsubscribe me / …), so a forwarded campaign footer is ignored. Subject-based detection (native Apple/Gmail List-Unsubscribe → subject "unsubscribe") is unchanged. `inboxStateManager` now calls the detector instead of inline keyword matching. Compliance: this only NARROWS matching for false positives — genuine requests (short reply, any imperative phrase, or the "unsubscribe" subject) still match, so no real opt-out is missed. Files: `backend/src/services/unsubscribeEnforcementService.ts`, `backend/src/services/inbox/inboxStateManager.ts`, NEW `backend/src/services/__tests__/detectInboxUnsubscribeIntent.test.ts`.
  - Verification: `npx jest detectInboxUnsubscribeIntent` — 10/10 pass (genuine: subject-unsub, short one-word reply, imperative phrase in a long rant, request above a quote; rejected: internal sender, quoted-footer-only, forwarded long campaign, empty). Type-check: TS 5.7.3 `tsc --noEmit` clean on touched files (zod/@types noise from the borrowed TS-4.9.5 worktree filtered; CI backend typecheck authoritative).

  - Date: 2026-07-16

A student could previously collect a video/testimonial/podcast card's points on a bare POST — no time was ever measured. Now: **accumulated play-time ÷ duration** (scrubbing to the end earns nothing) is measured client-side, ratcheted + clamped server-side, and completion is BLOCKED below the required share. Backend: (1) NEW pure `services/runtime/watchProgressMath.ts` (no model imports — unit-testable): `accumulateWatch` (clamp each delta ≤45s, ratchet watched_s/max_position_s/duration_s monotonically, cap watched_s at 2×duration, derive watched_pct 0..100), `isWatchableCard` (video metadata OR type∈{testimonial,podcast}), `requiredWatchPct` (card.completion_rules.video_watched → type completion_rules → DEFAULT 0.75; null=ungated — finally activating the dormant `completion_rules` vocabulary), `meetsWatchRequirement` (fail-OPEN when no duration was ever measurable so nobody is trapped). (2) NEW `services/runtime/watchProgressService.ts` composes the math with the DB: `recordWatchBeat` (findOrCreate progress + read-merge-update `timeline_card_progress.analytics.watch` JSONB, certificateService pattern; returns {watched_pct,required_pct,met}) + `assertWatchRequirement` (the gate; early-returns if already completed → idempotent, throws `{status:422,code:'watch_requirement',watched_pct,required_pct}` below threshold). (3) The gate is called in `progressionService.onCardCompleted` right after the card fetch, BEFORE the status flip + XP — one choke point covering the classroom drawer, Today, and the runtime. (4) NEW heartbeat endpoint `POST /api/portal/runtime/cards/:cardId/watch` (participant auth + a 60s/30 rate limiter) → `runtimeController.handleWatchBeat` (zod: delta_s 0..600, position/duration/provider optional). (5) `timelineController.handleCompleteCard` now passes status errors through (422 with watched_pct/required_pct) instead of flattening to 500. (6) Gate prerequisite: `runtimeService.openCard` now runs the same per-student `select*ForEnrollment` resolution the feed uses, so a random testimonial/podcast card opens in the workspace WITH its picked media (was `video:null` → would dead-end the gate). (8) `VideoEmbed.tsx` gains an optional `onWatchBeat` prop + internal accumulation (refs; folds only small position deltas — seeks add nothing; flushes ~every 15s of play + on pause/end/unmount): native timeupdate for <video>/<audio>, YouTube (`infoDelivery` postMessage) + Vimeo (`timeupdate` postMessage) player channels, visibility-gated dwell timer for Loom/Wistia/unknown; silent when the prop is absent (admin previews). (9) `runtimeApi.watch(cardId,beat)`. (10) `CardDetailBody.tsx` + `RuntimeWorkspace.tsx`: wire onWatchBeat → runtimeApi.watch, a watch-progress bar under the player ("Watched 43% · reach 75% to collect your points"), and a "Collect points"/"Mark complete" button DISABLED until the server reports `met` (also fixes the pre-existing gap: iframe videos had no completion affordance in the drawer). (11) `TodayShell.tsx` bug fix: its drawer onComplete never POSTed — now hits the classroom complete endpoint and lets a 422 propagate so the drawer surfaces "keep watching". ## INCIDENT — Cora inbox mail loop, 1,800+ emails sent in ~20 minutes (BC #10095332194)
- [x] Fix the Cora self-reply mail loop + add loop-guard defenses
  - Date: 2026-07-14
  - Session: CC-20260713-t3v8
  - What changed: Ali reported ~1,800 emails in ~20 minutes from Cora (the support@colaberry.com AI inbox agent, migrated from Relevance AI, `CORA_DRY_RUN` apparently flipped live in prod outside this repo's history). Investigated (via a read-only Explore subagent, then confirmed by hand) and found a real, fully explainable self-reinforcing loop, not the old external Relevance AI system (zero trace of it remains in this codebase). Root cause: Cora sends replies through the same Gmail account she reads from; the inbox sync pulled in **Sent mail too** (no folder filter), so her own reply got re-ingested ~60s later as "new" inbound mail; the "is this a Cora inquiry?" check did a raw substring match across **every email header**, not just delivery headers — and her own `From:` line contains `support@colaberry.com`, so she re-matched her own rule and replied to herself, forever. Nothing anywhere in the pipeline deduped by thread or capped send volume. Four fixes, all defense-in-depth (any one alone would have stopped this specific incident; together they close the whole class of bug): (1) `hardRuleEngine.ts`'s `cora_0c` rule now checks only `To`/`Cc`/`Delivered-To`/`X-Original-To` — never a raw header-blob substring match — plus an explicit guard that a message FROM Cora's own configured address can never match. (2) `inboxSyncService.ts`'s Gmail sync query gained `-in:sent` so her own outgoing replies are never re-ingested as inbound mail in the first place. (3) New `cora_reply_logs` table (unique on `thread_key`) backs a reserve-then-send dedup in `coraAgentService.ts::handleCoraInquiry` — the thread is reserved via `findOrCreate` *before* generating or sending anything, so a duplicate/re-ingested inquiry for an already-answered thread is skipped without ever calling OpenAI or Gmail. (4) A new circuit breaker (`CORA_CIRCUIT_BREAKER_MAX_SENDS`, default 20 per `CORA_CIRCUIT_BREAKER_WINDOW_MINUTES`, default 10) checks recent `cora_reply_sent` audit-log volume before any send; once tripped, everything routes to the human INBOX instead of sending — checked *before* the dedup reservation so a tripped thread stays available for a real attempt once volume subsides, rather than being permanently marked "already handled" with no reply ever sent. Also refactored `CORA_DRY_RUN` from a module-load-time cached constant to a per-call `isDryRun()` check — a safe, incidental improvement (flips take effect without a process restart) that also removed the need for `jest.resetModules()` gymnastics in the new tests. Files: NEW backend/src/models/CoraReplyLog.ts, backend/src/seeds/migrations/20260714_add_cora_reply_log.sql, backend/src/services/inbox/__tests__/coraAgentService.test.ts; backend/src/services/inbox/hardRuleEngine.ts (narrowed header check + self-send guard), backend/src/services/inbox/inboxSyncService.ts (`-in:sent`), backend/src/services/inbox/coraAgentService.ts (dedup reservation, circuit breaker, `isDryRun()`), backend/src/models/index.ts (CoraReplyLog wiring), backend/src/services/inbox/__tests__/hardRuleEngine.test.ts (new `evaluateHardRules` describe block for the Cora rule, including the exact loop regression).
  - Verification: backend `tsc --noEmit` clean. New/extended tests — `hardRuleEngine.test.ts` gained an `evaluateHardRules — Cora support inbox rule` block (7 tests: happy-path match via To/Delivered-To/X-Original-To, the exact regression — a message with Cora's own `From:` header no longer matches `cora_0c`, a message FROM the support address never matches even if also addressed back to itself, and the guard still applies under a `CORA_SUPPORT_ADDRESS` override). New `coraAgentService.test.ts` (10 tests: first-time-thread happy path, the loop regression itself — a duplicate thread is skipped without ever calling OpenAI or Gmail, thread-id-missing falls back to message-id, circuit breaker trips at the ceiling and does not trip below it, a send failure still routes to a human, and dry-run mode skips the circuit breaker but still dedupes). 37/37 passing across both files. Full backend suite: 182/185 passing (of 186; 1 pre-existing skip), same 3 pre-existing unrelated failures as every prior entry this session. Migration applied to local dev DB, table + unique constraint verified via `\d`. **Live verification against real running code, deliberately WITHOUT triggering any real OpenAI/Gmail send** (the nature of this incident made that the correct boundary, not a shortcut): rebuilt `accelerator-dev-backend`, confirmed the compiled `inboxSyncService.js` actually contains `-in:sent` in the query string, then called the real `evaluateHardRules()` directly — a simulated self-sent email (from the real configured `CORA_SUPPORT_ADDRESS`, with a `From:` header containing that same address) correctly returned `matched:false`, while a genuine inbound inquiry to the same address still correctly returned `rule_id:"cora_0c"` — proving the fix doesn't break the feature while closing the loop. Separately called the real `CoraReplyLog.findOrCreate` twice with the same `thread_key` against real Postgres: first call `created:true`, second call `created:false` with the identical row id — dedup proven at the database level, not just asserted in a mock. Circuit breaker behavior is covered by the 6 passing unit tests (mocked audit-log count) and was not additionally live-fired, since doing so meaningfully would require generating real audit-log volume without a clear safe way to do that without also risking a real send path.
  - Notes: `CORA_CIRCUIT_BREAKER_MAX_SENDS`/`CORA_CIRCUIT_BREAKER_WINDOW_MINUTES` are new optional env vars (default 20/10, no prod config change required to ship this fix). A generation or send failure leaves the thread's dedup reservation in place — deliberate: the existing `decideCoraDisposition` already routes those to the human INBOX, and auto-retrying a failed thread is exactly the class of risk this incident was about. This fix does not address whether the external Relevance AI integration is still active in parallel outside this codebase — that's outside this repo's visibility/control; confirming Relevance AI is fully decommissioned (or was never the actual source) is a separate action for Ali. Migration NOT yet applied to prod — this is the priority item to deploy once Kes/Ali confirm the immediate `CORA_DRY_RUN=true` mitigation is holding.

- [x] Build-log -> social drafter (#Colaberry stream) (BC #9985689786)
  - Date: 2026-07-14
  - Session: CC-20260713-t3v8
  - What changed: Ticket's Gherkin AC just says "produces a #Colaberry social draft" (singular), but its own "Build notes (precise)" line points to `TRAINING_INTEGRATION_PLAN.md` §3.7, which specifies 4 outputs (LinkedIn post, video script, architecture update, demo summary). First pass shipped text-only, reading the singular AC as "smallest version" — Kes corrected that this was my interpretation, not something the ticket said to defer, and asked for all 4. Rebuilt on that basis: each week's `BuildLogDraft` row (`project_id`+`week_number` unique) now holds 4 independently-generated, independently-approved sections (`linkedin_post`, `video_script`, `architecture_update`, `demo_summary`) inside `draft_content`, each with its own `{content, status, posted_at}` — dropped the earlier row-level `status`/`posted_at` columns entirely (redundant once status lives per-section; safe to change outright since this hadn't shipped anywhere). "A completed build-log entry" = a Tier-A `Artifact` row (`type:'build'`) in `submitted`/`reviewed` status — unchanged from the first pass. `draftBuildLogPost()` generates only whichever sections are still missing (per-section idempotency, not per-row): a section with existing content is never regenerated/re-billed; one section's LLM failure doesn't block the others (left ungenerated, retried next call); only throws if a call generates zero sections. `generateBuildLogDraftsForCompletedWeeks()` (weekly cron entry point, Mon 11:00 UTC) now skips a project/week only when *all 4* sections are done, otherwise fills in whatever's missing. `markBuildLogSectionStatus()` (renamed from `markBuildLogDraftStatus`) takes a `section` param, marks just that one posted/skipped, idempotent (re-posting doesn't bump `posted_at`), other sections untouched. Route `PATCH .../build-log-drafts/:draftId` now requires `{section, status}` in the body. No real LinkedIn/social API integration — "posted" stays a self-reported student action per the ticket's explicit no-auto-post trust control. Files: NEW backend/src/models/BuildLogDraft.ts, backend/src/services/buildLogDraftService.ts, backend/src/routes/buildLogDraftRoutes.ts, backend/src/seeds/migrations/20260714_add_build_log_drafts.sql, backend/src/__tests__/services/buildLogDraftService.test.ts; backend/src/models/index.ts (wiring + associations), backend/src/server.ts (route registration), backend/src/services/schedulerService.ts (new cron).
  - Verification: backend `tsc --noEmit` clean. `buildLogDraftService.test.ts` — 19/19 passing: all-4-sections happy path, `#Colaberry` normalization boundary, per-section idempotency (only missing sections regenerated, existing ones untouched — including a `posted` section staying `posted`), zero-LLM-call boundary when all 4 already exist, out-of-range week rejected pre-DB, missing project/incomplete week failure paths, one-section-fails-doesn't-block-the-others (failure isolation — the exact bug class this design targets), all-4-fail surfaces `UpstreamUnavailable` with no write, batch generator (drafts/skips-fully-done/isolates-per-project-failure), `markBuildLogSectionStatus` happy/idempotent/other-sections-untouched/unknown-section/missing-draft/not-yet-generated boundaries. Full backend suite: 3501/3602 passing (100 skipped), same 3 pre-existing unrelated failures as every prior entry this session (`seedCurriculumCourseLinks.test.ts`, `projectDnaService.test.ts`, `adminRoutes.test.ts`). **Caught a real production bug via live testing that the mocked unit tests could not have caught**: the first live-verification pass showed a genuine AI-drafted response in the HTTP body, but a direct `SELECT` against Postgres showed `content: null` for every section — the DB was never actually updated. Root cause: `draftBuildLogPost` read `draftRow.draft_content` by reference and mutated its nested fields in place before calling `.update()`; Sequelize's dirty-checking compares the incoming value against its own in-memory previous-value snapshot, and since both were now the same already-mutated object, it saw "no change" and silently skipped writing that column — the in-memory response looked correct while the database silently kept the stale `null` skeleton from the row's initial creation. Every re-run would have regenerated all 4 sections from scratch forever, burning 4 real LLM calls per call with zero persistence — exactly the kind of idempotency violation the repo's CLAUDE.md calls a production defect, not a nit. Fixed by deep-cloning (`JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(...))`) before mutating, so the object passed to `.update()` is never reference-identical to Sequelize's tracked previous value. Re-verified against real Postgres end-to-end: generated all 4 sections for a real project/week → confirmed via direct SQL that `content` was genuinely persisted (not just in the API response) → called generate again → `generated_at` and all content byte-identical before/after (true idempotency, zero re-billed LLM calls, confirmed via DB read not just HTTP response) → marked `linkedin_post` posted → `posted_at` set, `video_script` untouched → re-posted `linkedin_post` → `posted_at` unchanged (idempotent) → marked `video_script` skipped independently → `architecture_update`/`demo_summary` still `draft`, proving true per-section independence → invalid section name rejected 400 → a JWT for a different enrollment got `404` on the same project's drafts, confirming per-student isolation held through the rewrite. Migration dropped/recreated on local dev DB (`accelerator_dev1`) to match the new schema (row-level status/posted_at columns removed). The weekly cron's registration itself was not live-fired (`startScheduler()` gated behind `env.enableFollowUpScheduler`, off by design in dev to avoid also triggering the health monitor's real Synthflow voice call) — confirmed correct via `tsc` + structural match to neighboring cron blocks only.
  - Notes: This is now the full §3.7 scope — no formats remain deferred. No real LinkedIn/social API posting integration exists; "posted" is self-reported. Migration NOT yet applied to prod. Left the demo build-log draft and its source test artifact in the dev DB as legitimate feature-generated data. The Sequelize JSONB-mutation gotcha here (read-by-reference, mutate-in-place, then `.update()` silently no-ops) is worth remembering for any future JSONB field — mocked unit tests cannot catch it since a bare `jest.fn()` doesn't replicate real Sequelize change-detection; only a live DB round-trip surfaces it, which is why the live-verification step in this repo's process is load-bearing, not a formality.

    - **NEW `services/appPaymentReconcileService.ts`:** heals missed-webhook membership payments. For OUR checkout customers (enrollment carries a paysimple_customer_id we stored) that are still unpaid, it links their live PaySimple membership payment (>= $100; the $50 deposit stays a deposit).
