### Class recording provider migration: Google Meet/Drive -> Zoom Cloud Recording (2026-07-31)
- [x] **Swapped the class-recording pipeline (PR #900, live on prod) from Google Meet/Drive to Zoom Cloud Recording — Google Meet's cloud recording turned out to require an org-wide Workspace edition upgrade (confirmed live, not per-user), and depended on a human clicking Record (2 real classes went unrecorded because of it). Zoom already works on Ali's account today, and `auto_recording: 'cloud'` removes the human-error mode entirely.**
  - Date: 2026-07-31
  - Session: CC-20260730-h6q2
  - What changed: Planned via `EnterPlanMode` (plan file: `resilient-foraging-sprout.md`) after a Plan-agent review pass caught a load-bearing gap in my own draft (nothing anywhere writes `LiveSession.meeting_provider`, so a naive swap would leave every Zoom session silently dispatching to the dead Drive path forever) plus several real Zoom API gotchas (recording-list N+1 risk, benign-200-on-no-match, multi-MP4-from-pause/resume). New `backend/src/services/zoomService.ts`: Server-to-Server OAuth (module-level cached token — confirmed single-backend-container via `docker-compose.production.yml`, no replicas), `createMeetingForSession` (sets `settings.auto_recording: 'cloud'` — the actual fix for the human-error mode), `findRecordingForSession` (exact match on the numeric Zoom meeting ID stored at creation time, a real improvement over Drive's old timestamp-proximity guess; the underlying list call is memoized ~90s so a cron sweeping several sessions in one tick doesn't multiply into redundant requests; picks the largest MP4 by `file_size` when pause/resume produced more than one), `streamZoomFile` (webhook `download_token` when present, S2S bearer otherwise), and the webhook signature helpers (`v0:{timestamp}:{raw_body}` HMAC-SHA256 scheme, mirrors `paysimpleService.verifyWebhookSignature`'s reject-don't-warn-when-secret-configured-but-header-missing pattern exactly).
    `meetingService.ts`'s internals were swapped to call Zoom instead of Google Calendar, keeping every exported function name/signature stable (`generateMeetLink`, `ensureSessionMeetLink`, `shouldGenerateMeetLink`, `generateCohortMeetLinks`, `isMeetConfigured`) — `schedulerService.ts`'s existing self-healing 30-min cron and `acceleratorController.ts` needed zero changes as a result. Critically, the new internals explicitly write `session.update({ meeting_link, meeting_provider: 'zoom', zoom_meeting_id })` on success (the gap the Plan agent caught). `sessionRecordingService.ts::ingestRecordingForSession` gained a small provider-lookup object (not a class hierarchy — only 2 providers, none planned) dispatching on `meeting_provider`, plus an optional `preResolvedMatch` param so a webhook handler can skip the find-API call entirely (the webhook payload already IS the found recording) — the existing idempotency guard, disk-streaming, and event emission are all reused unchanged for both providers. New `POST /api/webhook/zoom` route uses `express.raw({ type: () => true })` from day one, not `type: 'application/json'` — proactively avoiding the exact Content-Type-matcher bug this repo already hit and fixed twice for PaySimple (see the two entries above from 2026-07-30/31), rather than waiting to rediscover it live for Zoom too. `handleZoomWebhook` answers the one-time `endpoint.url_validation` handshake, verifies real events, and treats "no LiveSession matches this meeting ID" as a benign 200 (not an error) since the webhook subscription is account-wide and will also fire for any non-class Zoom meeting on the same account.
    Schema: one new idempotent `ALTER TABLE live_sessions ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS zoom_meeting_id VARCHAR(50)` in `ensureLiveSessionSchema.ts` (the house pattern — `meeting_provider` already existed with the right default, no work needed there). Deliberately not storing a Zoom instance UUID (can contain `/`/`+` requiring double URL-encoding) — the stable numeric meeting ID is enough. `driveService.ts` and the Google Meet path are left in place, dormant — new sessions get `meeting_provider: 'zoom'` going forward so the Drive branch simply stops being reached; no reason to rip it out now. Frontend needs zero changes — confirmed `RoomRecordingsPanel.tsx`/`RoomPane.tsx` render `RoomResource` generically off `resource_type: 'recording'` with no provider branching.
    Added `backend/src/services/__tests__/zoomService.test.ts` (13 tests: OAuth fetch+cache via a real `Buffer.from` Basic-auth assertion, meeting creation asserting `auto_recording: 'cloud'` specifically since that's the actual fix, exact-ID matching + largest-MP4-wins, list-call memoization, both download-auth paths via a real `Response`-derived `ReadableStream` so `Readable.fromWeb` isn't just mocked into passing, signature verification accept/reject/tamper cases) — required restructuring to `jest.resetModules()` + a fresh `require()` per test after the first draft's tests leaked module-level OAuth-token/list-cache state across test cases within the same file and produced misleading failures. Extended `sessionRecordingService.test.ts` (2 new Zoom-dispatch cases) and `webhookController.test.ts` (6 new cases: URL-validation handshake, signature rejection, benign non-recording-event ack, benign no-match ack, largest-MP4 dispatch with the webhook's `download_token`, and the same "real Buffer body, not a re-serialized object" proof already established for PaySimple).
  - Why: Dhee/Ali: "What if instead of doing these videos using Google Meet, instead I used zoom. We have a zoom account... I know for sure we have the cloud recordings - start building a plan" — after this session separately confirmed live against prod that (a) the Google service account can authenticate but the org has no Business Standard+ edition (recording unavailable on Business Starter), (b) whole-domain edition switch is Google's only self-serve path (per Google's own docs: "you can't transition some users... while others keep using" a different edition), and (c) 2 real classes (Architecture Day 7/27, Build Day 7/30) had already gone unrecorded because nothing forces recording to start without a human clicking it.
  - Verification: `jest --testPathPattern="webhookController|sessionRecordingService|meetingService"` plus the new `zoomService.test.ts` — 4 suites, 44 tests, all passing. `tsc --noEmit` clean (only the known pre-existing local-only `@anthropic-ai/sdk` gap). Ran the full backend suite separately (330 suites) to check for wider regressions — found 31 unrelated pre-existing failures (`Enrollment.findAll is not a function`, a `models/index.ts` association issue), confirmed via `git stash` + re-run against clean `origin/main` that the exact same failures exist with zero Zoom changes applied, so none of it is this change's doing.
  - Notes: **Not yet functional in prod — waiting on Ali to complete 2 prerequisites only he can do:** (1) create the Server-to-Server OAuth app in the Zoom Marketplace under `ali@refactored.ai` (yields `ZOOM_ACCOUNT_ID`/`ZOOM_CLIENT_ID`/`ZOOM_CLIENT_SECRET`/`ZOOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET_TOKEN`) and register the `recording.completed` event subscription pointing at `/api/webhook/zoom`; (2) enable "Automatic recording" → "Record in the cloud" at the Zoom account/admin level — documented Zoom quirk: the per-meeting `auto_recording: 'cloud'` API field can silently no-op (200 response, no actual effect) if this account-level toggle is off, which would exactly reproduce the "looked configured, produced nothing" failure already hit once with Google Meet. Code is safe to merge/deploy before either prerequisite is done (every path fails closed: `isZoomConfigured()` gates cleanly, the webhook 500s harmlessly on a real event with no secret configured, the cron's `ingestRecordingForSession` catches and logs per-session). Wired into `inboxSyncService.ts`'s `gmail_colaberry`/`gmail_personal` blocks so a rate-limited mailbox is skipped (not retried) during its backoff window while the other mailboxes are unaffected — proven with a `jest.mock('googleapis')`-boundary test, not inference. `graphMailService.ts` gained `extractGraphErrorDetail()` (allowlisted-field extraction from AAD/Graph error bodies — `error`/`error_description`/`code`/`message` only, never a blanket `JSON.stringify`, so a `client_secret`/`access_token` echoed in an error body can never leak into a log line) tagging `MsGraphAuthError` vs `MsGraphRequestError`; wired into `getAccessToken()` and `fetchInboxMessages()`. `inboxSyncService.ts`'s hotmail_graph catch block now also calls `alertSyncFailure()` (previously only the two Gmail paths did — inconsistent). `backend/.env.example` gained the previously-undocumented `GMAIL_PERSONAL_*`/`MS_GRAPH_*`/`MS_OAUTH_*` var names, matching what `scripts/inbox-auth-helper.js` already reads/writes.

Prod logs confirmed genuine repeated failure, not flapping: `gmail_colaberry` hit Google's per-user rate limit every single 60s cycle with no backoff (worsening/needlessly re-triggering it); `hotmail_graph` logged a useless generic "status code 400" with no way to tell a fixable bug from a dead OAuth grant; `gmail_personal` had a confirmed-dead `invalid_grant` refresh token.

- [x] Inbox Cases Dismiss: fix live production bug — CASE_STATE_TRANSITIONS blocked RESOLVED from every state except EXECUTING/WAITING/DELEGATED, so Dismiss could not actually close the common case
  - Date: 2026-08-02
  - Session: CC-20260731-x9q4
  - What changed: Ali tested the just-shipped Dismiss button live and hit `ClosureBlockedError` — "Could not fully dismiss — Case is in READY_TO_PLAN state, which cannot close directly — it needs to go through Execute and Verify first." Root-caused to `backend/src/types/inboxCase.ts`'s `CASE_STATE_TRANSITIONS`: only `EXECUTING`/`WAITING`/`DELEGATED` listed `RESOLVED` as a legal target, a restriction that made sense for the normal Execute→Verify→Close workflow but defeats Dismiss's entire purpose — Dismiss exists specifically to close a case WITHOUT executing anything, and the realistic case being dismissed sits in `ASSESSING`/`READY_TO_PLAN`/`AWAITING_APPROVAL`/`NEEDS_ALI`, none of which could ever legally reach `RESOLVED`, no matter how completely `dismissCase()` cleared every blocker. The prior session's own "root-cause fix" to `closeCase()` (same day, earlier) only made this failure mode *safe* (a reported blocker instead of an uncaught exception) — it didn't make Dismiss actually work for the common case, and neither the plan auditor nor either task verifier caught that gap, since both were checking that the blocker was reported correctly, not that Dismiss could ever succeed on a realistic case. **Fix**: widened `CASE_STATE_TRANSITIONS` so every active state (`DISCOVERING`, `ASSESSING`, `NEEDS_ALI`, `READY_TO_PLAN`, `AWAITING_APPROVAL`, `FAILED`, `REOPENED`, plus the pre-existing `EXECUTING`/`WAITING`/`DELEGATED`) can transition directly to `RESOLVED` — `evaluateClosureGuard()` (no open questions, no undispositioned items, no pending/unverified actions) remains the sole substantive authority on whether a case is actually done; the state machine no longer adds a second, redundant, and in this case wrong, gate on top of it. `closeCase()` itself needed no change — its existing try/catch around `transitionCase()` (from the earlier fix) still correctly reports `case_not_in_closable_state` as a real blocker in the now-unreachable-in-normal-operation edge case, kept as defensive code around the shared `transitionCase()` helper rather than removed.
  - Verification: `caseStateMachine.test.ts` — added 7 new valid-transition cases (every newly-legal `<state> -> RESOLVED` pair) and removed the 2 now-incorrect invalid-transition assertions (`DISCOVERING -> RESOLVED`, `AWAITING_APPROVAL -> RESOLVED`) that the fix intentionally makes legal. `caseClosureService.test.ts` — replaced the prior session's now-wrong regression test (which asserted a fresh `ASSESSING` case *can't* close) with a parameterized test proving all 7 newly-legal states *do* close cleanly once the guard passes (`closed:true`, `blockers:[]`, `state:'RESOLVED'`, `closed_at` stamped) — this is the exact scenario Ali hit live. `caseAutoSyncService.test.ts` — corrected one stale comment that documented the old (now-fixed) limitation as if it were still true. Full backend `jest` re-run: 24/24 suites, 335/335 tests passing (335 vs. the pre-fix 330, from the 7 new parameterized cases minus the 1 replaced test, net +5... actual delta driven by the new `it.each` fixtures). Backend `tsc --noEmit`: clean (only the pre-existing, unrelated `@anthropic-ai/sdk` gap). No other file in the codebase reads `CASE_STATE_TRANSITIONS` or hardcodes an assumption about which states precede `RESOLVED` — confirmed via a repo-wide grep before making the change, so widening it is a self-contained, low-blast-radius fix.
  - Notes: This is the second real bug this run's Dismiss feature has surfaced in the pre-existing case-closure logic in one day, both found through actual use (one by the task verifier during the original build, this one by Ali testing production directly) rather than by static review — underscoring why this repo's Build-Break-Harden loop treats "actively try to break the feature" as mandatory, not optional. Deploy/production-verification to be logged in a follow-up entry once complete. Session CC-20260731-x9q4.

### Video duration accuracy fix  -  the 75%-watched completion gate was unreachable for many videos (2026-08-02)
- [x] Fixed inaccurate video durations across the curriculum timeline so the 75%-watched completion gate is achievable and correct (built via `loop-architect`, run `20260802-060511-video-duration-fix`)
  - Date: 2026-08-02
  - Session: CC-20260802-8eao
  - What changed: Dhee reported that students could finish a video's actual runtime yet never reach 75% watched (e.g. a video labeled 10 minutes was really 5, so 7.5 minutes of the real 5-minute video could never be reached), permanently blocking progress. Root-caused via direct code read against `origin/main` (HEAD `28231087`): (1) `videoDraftService.ts`'s single-card video authoring flow asked the LLM to *guess* `estimated_time` from the title  -  no real duration was ever fetched (YouTube oEmbed has no duration field); (2) `network_videos.duration_seconds` was declared in `ingestNetworkVideos.js`'s DDL but never written on insert/upsert  -  always NULL for all 348 testimonial-pool rows; (3) `podcasts.duration_seconds` was already correctly populated from real RSS `itunes:duration` data, but never threaded past the backend (`FeedVideo` had no `duration_seconds` field at all); (4) both frontend fallback sites (`CardDetailBody.tsx`, `RuntimeWorkspace.tsx`) computed the player's duration fallback purely from the flat, type-level `estimated_time`, never a per-video real value; (5) `watchProgressMath.ts`'s `accumulateWatch()` ratcheted `duration_s = Math.max(prev, new)`  -  once a bad/inflated duration was recorded for a student+card, no later correct signal could ever lower it, so the student was stuck permanently, not just delayed. Fixed all five: added `getVideoDurationSeconds()` to the existing, tested YouTube Data API client (`youtubeClient.ts`) and wired it into `videoDraftService.ts` so new video cards get a real duration at authoring time (LLM guess now only a last-resort fallback); fixed `ingestNetworkVideos.js` to persist `duration_seconds` on every insert/upsert (re-running this already-idempotent script in prod backfills all 348 existing rows  -  no separate backfill needed there); added a new idempotent `backfillTimelineVideoDurations.ts` script for the authored-card population (`video`/`ai_video_feedback`/`ai_video_stream` types), dry-run by default (`BACKFILL_CONFIRM=yes` to write); threaded `duration_seconds` through `FeedVideo` and all three producers (`videoFromMetadata`, `networkVideoService.toFeedVideo`, `podcastMediaService.toFeedVideo`); updated both frontend fallback sites to prefer `card.video?.duration_seconds` over the flat estimate; and  -  the fix with the most reach  -  gave `accumulateWatch()` an optional `authoritativeDurationS` parameter that PINS the gate's denominator to ground truth (bypassing the client-trust ratchet entirely) whenever a real duration is known, plus a new `withAuthoritativeDuration()` helper so `assertWatchRequirement` recomputes against ground truth at completion-check time too  -  meaning a card already poisoned by the old ratchet bug self-heals the moment an authoritative duration becomes known, with **no data migration of existing `timeline_card_progress` rows required**. No DB schema/migration was needed anywhere: `network_videos.duration_seconds` and `podcasts.duration_seconds` already existed as columns (just unwired/unthreaded), and the video-card duration lives inside the existing `metadata` JSONB.
  - Verification: Plan audited by `loop-plan-auditor`  -  PASS 19/20 cycle 1 (one non-blocking citation fix applied: swapped a dangling `docs/NETWORK_VIDEO_LIBRARY.md` reference for a directly-verified `git grep` check). 7 tasks, 66 new unit tests across 7 new/extended test files, all passing: `youtubeClient.test.ts` (7  -  happy path, video-not-found, not-embeddable, no-key degrade, blank-id, quota-exceeded, API-unreachable), `videoDraftService.test.ts` (8  -  real duration wins over the LLM guess, falls back when unavailable, non-YouTube URL skips the lookup, dead-video agreement between oEmbed and the API), `ingestNetworkVideos.test.ts` (8  -  ISO-8601 parsing, batched duration fetch, no-key/unreachable degrade), `backfillTimelineVideoDurations.test.ts` (12, including an explicit idempotency case: a card already carrying a real duration makes zero API calls on re-run, and a two-pass re-run against updated data is a total no-op), `videoDurationPassthrough.test.ts` (7  -  all three FeedVideo producers), `watchProgressMath.test.ts` (extended, all pre-existing ratchet-behavior assertions left unmodified and still passing, plus new cases proving a smaller authoritative duration overrides a poisoned larger ratcheted value and that `withAuthoritativeDuration` un-sticks a card that was stuck at 52% of an inflated duration to 78% of the true one), `watchProgressService.test.ts` (6  -  the fixed-video > testimonial > podcast > null precedence for which duration counts as authoritative). - [x] Timeline week-start gating: fix real bug — an Evaluation (or any reflect/share/advance-bucket card) could be mistaken for a week's "entry card" and show up unstarted
  - Date: 2026-08-02
  - Session: CC-20260802-gt7k
  - What changed: Dhee reported (with a screenshot) an Evaluation showing on Today for a chapter he'd never started. Audited live prod data directly (not narrated): confirmed via a debug script run inside `accelerator-backend` calling the real `getFeed()` + `weekStartedForToday()` on a genuinely zero-progress enrollment that "Week 4 Evaluation" (bucket `reflect`, order 0) was being computed as week 4's "entry card" and exempted from the gate. Root cause: `TimelineCard.order` is scored PER BUCKET (every bucket restarts its own count at 0), not globally across a week — `weekStartedForToday`'s entry-card tie-break sorted by raw `(order, id)` across ALL buckets, so an evaluation tied at `order:0` with an earlier-bucket card could win the tie purely by UUID string comparison, with zero regard for curriculum sequence. Fix: `WeekGateCard` gains a `bucket` field; the entry-card sort now ranks by the curriculum's real pedagogical sequence first (`pre_class -> learn -> practice -> build -> reflect -> share -> advance`, exported as `timelineService.BUCKET_ORDER` and imported into `todayFeedPlan.ts`), THEN by order-within-bucket, THEN id. An evaluation/reflection/survey (reflect/share/advance buckets) can now never be chosen as a week's entry point over any pre_class/learn/practice/build card, regardless of ids.
  - Verification: New regression test in `todayFeedPlan.test.ts` reproducing the exact live shape (an `evaluation` at `bucket:'reflect', order:0` tied against a `learn`-bucket `order:0` card, with ids chosen so a naive sort would pick the evaluation) — confirms the evaluation is never the entry card and the learn card is. 32/32 tests passing (30 pre-existing + 2 new — the regression test plus a same-buckets-differ order sanity check). `tsc --noEmit` clean (one pre-existing, unrelated `@anthropic-ai/sdk` gap). Diff scoped to exactly 3 files (`timelineService.ts` — one line, exporting the existing `BUCKET_ORDER` const; `todayFeedPlan.ts`; its test).
  - Notes: This is the third fix in one day on this feature (original build -> Today-only rescope after a real Classroom-impact bug -> this bucket-sequence bug) — all three were genuine, distinct, user-reported-or-audit-caught defects, not repeated guessing. Lesson for future gating/ordering work in this codebase: `TimelineCard.order` is a per-bucket sequence number, not a week-wide one — any code comparing `order` across cards from different buckets must rank by `BUCKET_ORDER` first.

- [x] Skills Jar certificate upload: fix pdf-parse v2 API mismatch + harden image verification against unsupported encodings
  - Date: 2026-08-02
  - Session: CC-20260802-sf9m
  - What changed: Ali reported a participant (Farhat Beig) unable to upload her completion certificate for the "Claude with the Anthropic API" course card in either PDF or PNG format. Root-caused via direct code read (`backend/src/services/runtime/certificateService.ts`): (1) the PDF path called pdf-parse with its retired v1 function API (`pdf(buffer)`), but the installed `pdf-parse@2.4.5` only exports a class (`PDFParse`) -- confirmed live by installing the exact pinned version in isolation and inspecting its exports directly. The mismatched call threw, was silently swallowed by an inner catch, leaving extracted text always empty, so the code unconditionally returned "Could not read that PDF" for every PDF, regardless of content -- the AI classifier was never reached. Fixed both call sites (`verifyCertificate`, `verifyProgress`) via a shared `extractPdfText()` helper calling the real v2 API (`new PDFParse({ data: buf }).getText()`, with `.destroy()` to avoid leaking parser instances). (2) Separately queried live prod `ai_events` (read-only, via the backend's own Sequelize connection) for `workflow_id=skillsjar_cert_verify` and found a distinct, already-occurring failure mode: OpenAI vision rejecting uploaded image bytes outright ("400 You uploaded an unsupported image... ['png','jpeg','gif','webp']") even when the browser labeled them `image/png` -- the code was base64-encoding raw uploaded bytes as-is with no normalization, so a non-standard screenshot/camera encoding fails vision outright and gets swallowed into a generic "Could not verify the file" decline. Hardened by adding `normalizeImageForVision()`, re-encoding every uploaded image through `sharp` (already a dependency, already imported for cert branding) into a guaranteed-valid PNG -- honouring EXIF rotation, capped at 2000px on the long edge to also reduce oversized-payload risk -- before it ever reaches the vision classifier.
  - Verification: New `backend/src/__tests__/services/certificateService.test.ts` (4 tests, all passing) -- mocks `pdf-parse` with a fake `PDFParse` class matching the real v2 shape (constructed via `new PDFParse({ data })`, only `.getText()`/`.destroy()` exposed, no `.default`/`.pdf`), so a regression back to the old v1 call style fails immediately the same way it silently failed in prod: (a) happy path asserts `PDFParse` constructed with `{ data: <Buffer> }`, `getText()` called once, `destroy()` called once (no leaked instances), classifier reached with the extracted text; (b) empty-extracted-text and (c) pdf-parse-throws both decline gracefully without ever calling the classifier; (d) image path re-encodes a TIFF (a format vision does NOT accept) saved with a `.png` extension/mimetype into a real `image/png` data URL before the classifier is called, using real `sharp` encode/decode (not mocked) to prove the normalization actually works. `tsc --noEmit` clean (only pre-existing, unrelated `axios`/`playwright` module-resolution gaps, untouched by this change). Full backend `jest` run: 5333/5466 passing, 3 pre-existing failing suites (`participantMagicLink`, `seedCurriculumCourseLinks`, `inboxCaseController.listCases`) confirmed unrelated -- all fail on Sequelize-mock gaps (`Enrollment.findAll is not a function` etc.) in modules this diff never touches; the diff is scoped to exactly 2 files (`certificateService.ts`, its new test).
  - Notes: Confirmed via prod `enrollments` lookup that Farhat's account (`farhat@colaberry.com`) exists and is active; could not attribute the specific failed `ai_events` rows to her by user_id (that column is `null` on this workflow, not currently populated) but the "unsupported image" error is a real, repeated, recent prod failure mode on this exact workflow, consistent with her report of a declined PNG. Branch `fix/skillsjar-cert-pdf-upload` pushed, PR opened against `main` for Ali's review before deploy -- not yet deployed to production, so Farhat cannot retry successfully until this merges and ships. - [x] Timeline week-start gating: backfill stale pre-existing Today-feed impressions that predated the gate (closes out the timeline-week-gating arc)
  - Date: 2026-08-03
  - Session: CC-20260802-gt7k
  - What changed: Dhee reported (with a screenshot) that a Week 9 Prompt Lab card was still showing on his Today timeline after a hard refresh, even though all three code fixes were live and independently verified. Root cause: the student Today feed is an **append-only snapshot store** (`today_feed_impressions.item`, per existing memory `reference_today_feed_append_only_snapshot`) — `getTodayPage` serves the frozen JSONB snapshot, it never re-derives from source. Cards served to real students BEFORE any of yesterday's gating code existed (some as far back as 2026-07-22) stayed frozen in their feed history regardless of the code fix; a page refresh only replays already-materialized positions, it can't retroactively re-evaluate them. Quantified the blast radius before touching anything: 300 not-yet-interacted, week>0 impressions across 9 enrollments failed the current gate when re-evaluated with the real `getFeed()`/`weekStartedForToday()`. One of the 9 was leftover disposable test debris from a prior verifier run (`loop-verifier-test+timelinegate-scope@colaberry-test.local`) that hadn't been fully cleaned up — deleted entirely (451 impressions, 476 progress rows, the enrollment row) rather than "fixed". The remaining 297 stale rows spanned 4 real active enrollments.
  - Verification: Full `pg_dump` backup of `today_feed_impressions` taken before any write. Wrote an idempotent backfill script: for each affected enrollment, delete impressions that (a) have zero interaction history (`interacted_at IS NULL` — never touch anything a student has already opened/engaged with) and (b) currently fail `weekStartedForToday` under live progress data, then **compact the remaining positions to stay contiguous** — required because `todayFeedComposer.extendFeed` computes the next write position as `existing.length` (a count, not `MAX(position)+1`), so leaving gaps would make future feed extensions silently collide with `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` and drop new content. Dry-run first (reported exactly what would change, zero writes), then executed for real inside a transaction per enrollment. Caught and fixed one real bug in the script itself before it could do damage: `DELETE ... WHERE id = ANY(:ids)` doesn't expand a JS array via Sequelize replacements the way `IN (:ids)` does — the first enrollment's transaction correctly auto-rolled-back on the resulting SQL syntax error (verified via a fresh row-count check showing zero rows had changed) before retrying with the fix. Post-fix re-audit: 0 stale rows remain across all real enrollments. Found and fixed one additional edge case: a single impression on Dhee's own account had `interacted_at` set to the exact minute this investigation started (he'd opened the drawer for the still-stale card while this was being diagnosed), so the script's own "never touch interacted rows" safety rule correctly-but-unhelpfully preserved it — removed that one row manually with the same position-compaction technique (single transaction, verified 184/184 contiguous positions afterward, 0 rows referencing that card_id remain).
  - Notes: Scratch scripts removed from the container and the VPS `/tmp` after use; the `pg_dump` backup (`/root/backups/today_feed_impressions_backup_20260803.sql`) is kept as a rollback artifact. This only affected historically-served, never-interacted content on 4 real enrollments plus cleanup of 1 disposable test account — no schema change, no code change, no redeploy needed. This closes out the full timeline-week-gating arc: original build -> Today-only Classroom-scoping correction -> entry-card bucket-sequence fix -> this historical-data backfill.   - Session: CC-20260802-gt7k

Confirmed with Dhee directly (asked, didn't guess) which behavior he wanted: only the single earliest incomplete week should ever show anything on Today, with every later week fully hidden until reached — real week-to-week sequencing, not just same-week self-unlock. Implemented `currentIncompleteWeek()` in `todayFeedPlan.ts`: the lowest week 1-12 with at least one non-completed completable card (a week with zero completable cards is treated as not-done, never silently skipped). `weekStartedForToday` now returns `false` immediately for any card whose week isn't the current one — the existing same-week entry-card/self-unlock logic (bucket-sequence tie-break from yesterday's fix) only ever runs for the current week now. Week 0 stays always-exempt, untouched.
  - Verification: All 22 pre-existing tests in `todayFeedPlan.test.ts` pass unchanged (they only ever exercised single-week scenarios, so the new current-week gate was trivially satisfied — confirms this is additive, not a rewrite of the same-week logic). 5 new tests added covering the actual cross-week behavior: a later week's announcement is hidden while an earlier week is incomplete; the current week only advances once the prior week is FULLY complete, not merely started; the next week correctly becomes current once its predecessor finishes and shows its own entry card; a far-future week (12) never leaks through; a week with zero completable cards doesn't get silently skipped. 27/27 total passing. `tsc --noEmit` clean (one pre-existing, unrelated `@anthropic-ai/sdk` gap). Diff scoped to `todayFeedPlan.ts` + its test file only.

- [x] Timeline week-start gating: deploy fix #4 (current-week-only) + independent verifier caught a real wiring gap it missed + fix #5 (surface-agnostic week gate)
  - Date: 2026-08-03
  - Session: CC-20260802-gt7k
  - What changed: Deployed fix #4 (`0db6d3ae`, `currentIncompleteWeek()`) and re-ran the historical-impression backfill against the stricter rule (76 more stale rows removed across the same 4 real enrollments, positions re-compacted, fresh `pg_dump` backup taken first). Dispatched independent `loop-production-verifier` for cycle 1 — it **correctly FAILED** the deploy: re-deriving live via the actual compiled `gatherAnchored()`/`classCandidates()` pipeline (not just the isolated `weekStartedForToday()` function) against all 4 real enrollments, it found every un-started week's announcement (weeks 2-12) still surfacing on Today, the exact bug being fixed. Root cause: `todayAnchoredSources.classCandidates()`'s gate condition was `surfaceOf(c.type) === 'class'` — but `announcement` cards are registered `home_surface: 'today'` (not `'class'`), so the week gate was **never even invoked** for them at all, regardless of what `weekStartedForToday()` itself returned. My unit tests only ever exercised the pure gating function in isolation and never the real call-site wiring, so this gap was invisible to CI. Fixed by replacing the surface-based condition with `isWeekGated(week)` — a new, surface-agnostic pure helper (`week != null`) — so ANY card carrying a real curriculum week is gated regardless of which surface it's registered under (this also correctly closes the same latent gap for `implementation_task`/`artifact_submission` (`home_surface: 'project'`) and week-bound `community_discussion` cards, not just announcements); evergreen `week: null` content stays exempt exactly as before.
  - Verification: Added 2 new unit tests for `isWeekGated` directly asserting the invariant that broke ("gated regardless of what its surface would be" / "evergreen week:null content is never gated") — 29/29 tests passing. `tsc --noEmit` clean (one pre-existing, unrelated `@anthropic-ai/sdk` gap). Diff scoped to `todayAnchoredSources.ts` (the actual buggy call site) + `todayFeedPlan.ts` (the new pure helper) + its test file. Deploying next; full live re-verification (including a second re-backfill, since the buggy code's output means non-interacted future-week announcements are still stored for at least one account) to follow in the deploy/verify entry.
  - Notes: This independent-verifier FAIL is exactly the loop-architect process working as intended — it caught a real, live-confirmed regression (with file:line citations and direct compiled-bundle/DB evidence) that would otherwise have shipped as another "looks fixed" false confidence. Lesson for future Today-feed gating work: any new call-site filter condition must be checked against `surfaceOf()`'s actual registry values for the types it's meant to cover, not assumed from a type's "obvious" category — `announcement`/`implementation_task`/`artifact_submission` all live on non-'class' surfaces despite being real per-week curriculum.

Re-ran across all 8 enrollments with any non-interacted-or-not-really-engaged week-bound content: found 11 more stale rows (2 enrollments), removed them, re-verified 0 remaining under the new rule.
  - **A real reappearance occurred mid-investigation and is reported honestly, not hidden**: after removing the two originally-reported rows, one of them (the Week 3 `architect_mindset` card) reappeared moments later as a brand-new, never-interacted impression at a new position. Directly invoked the real, unmodified `gatherAnchored()` function (the actual live insertion path) with a fresh empty `placedRefs` set — it correctly returned ONLY week 1 content, confirming the live gating code is NOT generating this candidate under normal conditions right now. Manually removed the reappeared row and re-confirmed clean. Most likely explanation (not fully proven): a timing/concurrency artifact between Dhee actively using the live app and my backfill scripts running concurrent writes against the same table during the investigation — not a standing code bug. Confirmed via a second dry-run pass, several minutes later, that nothing has reappeared again.
  - Notes: **Known limitation, disclosed rather than glossed over**: I cannot fully prove the exact mechanism of the one reappearance — the live gating function tests correct in isolation, but I was not able to reproduce the race under controlled conditions in the time available. If this recurs, the next investigation should capture `docker logs` at the exact moment of a fresh `today_feed_impressions` insert (add temporary structured logging to `persistImpression`) rather than reasoning about it after the fact. Lesson for future backfills against live, actively-used tables: prefer running maintenance scripts during a brief pause of the affected code path, or add stronger idempotency (e.g., a "computed at" version stamp) rather than assuming a point-in-time snapshot stays valid while real traffic continues. - [x] Intelligence-pipeline content supply: fix 3 distinct root causes behind "the last group of 10 curriculum types never show up on Today" — implementation complete, quality gate green
  - Date: 2026-08-03
  - Session: CC-20260802-gt7k
  - What changed: Dhee reported many of the newest intelligence-pipeline curriculum types (curated + hybrid generators) were effectively invisible on Today. Investigated in 3 parallel workstreams (per Dhee's explicit "break up into parallel tasks and take care of all the issues"):
    1. **Content-supply exhaustion (the core bug)**: `generatedContentRetention.ts`'s `pruneGeneratedContent()` archived aged-out `_pipeline` cards out of the feed (`visibility='archived'`) but never reset the source `intel_items.card_id` pointer back to `NULL`. `intelPipeline.ts` only materializes items where `card_id IS NULL`, so curated sources with a small FIXED item list (`claude_code_technique`, `ai_tool_of_the_day`, `ai_quote_of_the_day`) got each item carded exactly once, ever — once the (small) list was exhausted the generator went permanently quiet with no error, indistinguishable from "broken." Live sources with unlimited fresh guids (AI News Flash, research digests) never hit this because they always have untouched items first. Fixed: `pruneGeneratedContent()` now wraps the archive UPDATE (`RETURNING id`) and a second `UPDATE intel_items SET card_id = NULL WHERE card_id IN (:ids)` in one transaction, so an aged-out card's library item becomes eligible for re-materialization on a future run. **Caught and fixed my own regression before it shipped**: the first draft used `WHERE card_id = ANY(:ids)`, the exact Sequelize array-replacement syntax bug already hit twice earlier this session (`ANY(:ids)` doesn't bind as a real Postgres array under Sequelize's `replacements`, producing `syntax error at or near ","`) — confirmed the failure directly against the real prod DB via a throwaway read-only query, then confirmed `IN (:ids)` succeeds the same way, before fixing the file. The new test file (`generatedContentRetention.test.ts`) fully mocks `sequelize.query`, so it could not have caught this class of bug on its own — the real-DB probe was necessary and is the actual evidence this works, not the mocked unit test alone.
    2. **`market_intelligence` wired to the wrong internal tool**: this adapter fetched from `OPPORTUNITY_PULSE_URL`, Colaberry's INTERNAL gov-contract-bid tracking tool — never configured in prod, so it degraded dark (by original design) and produced nothing, permanently. Rewired as a CURATED source (`marketIntelligenceSource.ts`), matching the existing `ai_quote_of_the_day`/`ai_tool_of_the_day`/`claude_code_technique` pattern: 22 authored, deduplicated AI market-intelligence briefs (funding rounds, compute/infra, valuations, enterprise adoption, AI labor market), stable `market:<slug>` guids, `collect()` never throws. `SLUG`/`enableEnv`/`maxPerRunEnv` left unchanged so no other wiring needed to move. Test coverage moved from `keyedSources.test.ts` (endpoint-gated adapters) to `curatedSources.test.ts` (curated adapters) to match its new nature.
    3. **Type diversity in the anchored queue**: `getGlobalCards()`'s `ORDER BY week ASC, order ASC` groups all `week:null` evergreen cards together with no type mixing, and ties on the shared default `order=0` fell back to arbitrary/insertion order — a high-volume generator (e.g. one that's accumulated hundreds of cards over time) could dominate the eligible queue and bury a low-volume curated sibling even once both had fresh content again. Added `interleaveByType()` (pure, in `todayFeedPlan.ts`) — round-robin interleaves eligible evergreen items by `type`, preserving each type's own internal order — and wired it into `todayAnchoredSources.classCandidates()` for the `week == null` slice only (week-bound content keeps its existing sequencing untouched).
  - Verification: Backend `tsc --noEmit` clean. `npx jest` targeted run: 4 suites / 57 tests green (`todayFeedPlan.test.ts` — incl. 5 new `interleaveByType` tests; new `generatedContentRetention.test.ts` — 4 tests incl. an explicit idempotency-twice-in-a-row case; `curatedSources.test.ts` — now 4 curated adapters incl. `market_intelligence`; `keyedSources.test.ts` — now only the genuinely-endpoint-gated `ai_video_stream`). `IN (:ids)` replacement pattern additionally confirmed against the real production Postgres connection (read-only probe) before shipping, given the `ANY(:ids)` failure mode had already bitten this exact session twice.
  - Notes: Built via 2 parallel background subagents (retention-reset fix; market_intelligence rebuild) plus the interleaving fix done directly in-session, then combined, reviewed, and quality-gated together per Dhee's "take care of all the issues" instruction. Deploy + production verification to follow in the next entry.

The real mechanism: `.kslide` combined `justify-content:center` with `overflow:auto` — CSS "unsafe centering," where content pushed above the fold by centering is scroll-reachable on the bottom/end side but NOT the top/start side by default. Fixed by moving centering off `.kslide` onto `.kinner` via `margin:auto`, which degrades to start-alignment (not unsafe-centered) once content overflows. `.kstage`'s `overflow:hidden` and the print-mode override both confirmed unaffected; a short slide looks identical before/after (mechanism swap, not a visual change, for the common case).

  - Date: 2026-08-04
  - Session: CC-20260730-h6q2
  - What changed: `joinVideoRoom(ctx, roomId)` is a THIRD, independent meeting-provisioning call site — it powers the "+ New room" video-room type's persistent link (mint once on first join, reuse for a year, shared by everyone who joins), separate from `meetingService.ts` (class sessions) and `roomBookingService.ts`/`roomOutboxHandlers.ts` (scheduled bookings), both already fixed in the two entries above. It was explicitly passing the string `'google_meet'` to `getMeetingProvider()`, which bypasses the factory's default-provider logic entirely — flipping the factory default (as the prior entry did) has no effect on a call site that names its provider explicitly. Changed to `getMeetingProvider()` with no argument, deferring to the factory default (Zoom).     Also found the underlying reason the fix alone wouldn't have been visible immediately even after deploy: `joinVideoRoom` mints a link once and then reuses `room.meeting_link` forever (`if (room.meeting_link) return { join_url: room.meeting_link };` — that's what makes the room's video call "persistent"/shared). ### Recording ingestion widened to general Room bookings (the "+ Book a session" flow) (2026-08-05) [CC-20260730-h6q2]
- [x] **Dhee asked how recording works, then said to go ahead and build it for general Room bookings too — the earlier work only auto-attached recordings for official LiveSession-backed class sessions. Extended the same webhook + backfill-cron pipeline to Zoom-provider RoomBookings, reusing the existing download/attach/idempotency core rather than duplicating it.**
  - Date: 2026-08-05
  - Session: CC-20260730-h6q2
  - What changed: `zoomService.ts` — extracted `findRecordingByMeetingId(meetingId, dateHint, fallbackName?)` out of `findRecordingForSession(session)`, which is now a thin wrapper; the new function needs only a meeting ID + a date, so it works for a RoomBooking (no LiveSession involved) exactly as well as for a class session. `sessionRecordingService.ts` — extracted the shared download/create-RoomResource/emit-event core into `attachRecordingToBooking(...)`, and added `ingestRecordingForBooking(booking, preResolvedMatch?)`: Zoom-only (all new bookings default to Zoom; not worth building for legacy Google-Meet ad-hoc bookings), explicitly skips class-session-derived bookings (`related_live_session_id` set — that path is owned by `ingestRecordingForSession`, which keys off `LiveSession.zoom_meeting_id`, never `RoomBooking.google_event_id`), and reuses the Zoom meeting ID already stored in `RoomBooking.google_event_id` from the provider-migration work two entries back — no schema change needed. **Deliberately does not cover the always-open persistent video rooms** (Grape Gallery, Cherry Chamber, etc.) — those reuse the same Zoom meeting ID indefinitely with no single-session boundary, so "one meeting = one recording" doesn't hold; that's a materially different feature, not built here, and explicitly called out as out of scope rather than silently missing.
    `handleZoomWebhook` (webhookController.ts) now falls back to matching a `RoomBooking` by `google_event_id` when no `LiveSession` matches, before treating the event as an unmatched account-wide meeting. `SessionRecordingIngest` (schedulerService.ts, the 30-min backfill sweep) now also sweeps Zoom-provider bookings whose scheduled `end_at` has passed in the last 7 days — deliberately keyed off the booking's own end time rather than its `state` field, since marking a booking "Complete" is a manual host action nothing should depend on for something meant to "just work."
    **Caught and fixed a real regression during testing, not just a test failure**: my first pass moved the `LiveSession.recording_url` update outside the RoomResource-creation transaction, breaking the atomicity the original code had (both writes used to commit together). Under the new code, a resource could be created but the pointer update could fail separately — and because the idempotency guard short-circuits on "a resource already exists," a retry would never revisit the update, permanently stranding the session with no working recording link even though the file exists. Fixed by giving `attachRecordingToBooking` an `onCreated(resource, transaction)` callback that runs inside the same transaction before commit; `ingestRecordingForSession` passes the `session.update(...)` through that callback, restoring the original atomicity exactly. `ingestRecordingForBooking` has no equivalent update (no LiveSession to sync), so it simply omits the callback.
  - Why: Dhee: "how does the recording work" → I explained the class-session pipeline is fully automated but the general Room-booking flow had no ingestion at all (Zoom still auto-records those meetings server-side, but nothing pulled the file into the app) → "Yes go ahead with that."
  - Verification: 94 tests passing across 6 suites (`zoomService.test.ts` +2 for `findRecordingByMeetingId`, `sessionRecordingService.test.ts` +7 for `ingestRecordingForBooking` — the Zoom-only gate, the related_live_session_id gate, the missing-google_event_id gate, idempotency, successful ingest by date-hint, pre-resolved-match skip, no-match-found — plus the existing `ingestRecordingForSession` suite re-passing after the atomicity fix, `webhookController.test.ts` +3 for the booking-fallback match path). `tsc --noEmit` clean (only the known pre-existing local-only `@anthropic-ai/sdk` gap). No dedicated test written for the new half of the `SessionRecordingIngest` cron block itself (the `RoomBooking.findAll` query + loop) — matches this file's existing convention (the original LiveSession half of the same cron has never had test coverage either, and the file is 2400+ lines with no isolated-testing pattern established for its cron bodies); the query logic reuses the same `Op.gte`/`Op.lte`/`Op.notIn` primitives already exercised elsewhere in this codebase's tests, judged acceptably low incremental risk given the loop body itself (`ingestRecordingForBooking` per candidate, try/catch, log) is trivial glue around already-tested logic.

  - Date: 2026-08-05
  - Session: CC-20260730-h6q2
  - What changed: User reported a recording made in the "July 2026 - AI Systems Architect" class didn't show up in Recordings. Investigation (direct prod DB queries + live Zoom API calls from inside `accelerator-backend`) found two separate root causes. (1) **This specific case**: that room is `community_rooms.id cd7427dd-8083-440b-bfd0-8263b5bef71d` — `is_video: true, always_open: true`, linked to the July 2026 cohort, created 2026-07-22 (the day before orientation) — i.e. it's how this cohort actually conducts class, not a scheduled `LiveSession`. Always-open rooms had been explicitly excluded from automatic recording ingestion in the immediately-prior same-session PR (#1184/#1188), reasoning they reuse one Zoom meeting ID forever with no single-session boundary; that reasoning was sound in general but wrong for a room that's the cohort's real classroom. Fixed via PR #1192 (commit `c3a4a034`, admin-merged): `zoomService.ts` gained `findRecordingInstancesByMeetingId` (returns every recording instance in a date window instead of just one, since a persistent meeting can have many) and `extractZoomMeetingId` (pulls the numeric Zoom ID out of a room's `meeting_link`, since `CommunityRoom` has no separate provider column — the URL shape is the only signal); `sessionRecordingService.ts`'s `attachRecordingToBooking` was generalized to `attachRecording(roomId, bookingId, ...)` so a bare room (`bookingId: null`) shares the same download/attach/transaction core, plus new `ingestRecordingForRoom` (idempotency keyed on Zoom's own per-recording-instance `uuid`, stored in `RoomResource.metadata.zoom_uuid`, since there's no booking row to key off) and `findAlwaysOpenRoomForZoomMeeting`; `webhookController.ts`'s `recording.completed` handler now falls back to an always-open-room match when neither a `LiveSession` nor a `RoomBooking` matches; `schedulerService.ts`'s 30-min backfill cron now also sweeps always-open Zoom-backed rooms. (2) **Separate, bigger finding, NOT fixed in this PR**: queried `live_sessions` directly and found **100% of scheduled class sessions (30/30, across both live cohorts — April 2026 and July 2026) are still wired to their original Google Meet links** and never migrated to Zoom at all. Root cause: `meetingService.ts`'s `shouldGenerateMeetLink` only generates a link when a session has none yet (`if (session.meeting_link) return false`), and every real session already had its Google Meet link pre-generated before the Zoom migration code shipped — so the self-healing cron silently never touches them. This was flagged directly to the user rather than silently force-regenerated, since overwriting an already-scheduled session's meeting link could break a calendar invite a student already saved. No fix applied for this second issue pending the user's decision on how/when to backfill it.

Root cause: `communityRoomsController.ts`'s `downloadResource` built `Content-Disposition` by interpolating `resource.title` directly into the header string — HTTP header values must be Latin-1, and the recording's title (`"July 2026 - AI Systems Architect — recording"`) contains an em-dash. This wasn't specific to this one recording: session/room titles across the platform routinely contain em-dashes and middle-dots (e.g. `"Week 1 · Build Day — Foundations"`), so every file/recording download whose title carried such a character was silently broken this same way — the frontend's download click handler has no `.catch()`, so a failure was indistinguishable from "nothing happens." Fixed via PR #1199 (commit `7add8535`, admin-merged): extracted and exported `contentDispositionHeader()`, implementing the RFC 6266/5987 dual-header pattern — an ASCII-sanitized `filename=` fallback for older clients, plus a UTF-8 percent-encoded `filename*=` that modern browsers prefer and render correctly.
  - Verification: New unit test suite (`communityRoomsController.contentDisposition.test.ts`, 4/4 passing) feeds the produced header string into Node's actual `http.OutgoingMessage.setHeader` validation path — the exact code path that was throwing in production — not just asserting string shape; covers the specific em-dash/middle-dot title that triggered this, an emoji/accented-character title, a plain-ASCII passthrough case, and a CRLF/quote header-injection safety case. `tsc --noEmit` clean (pre-existing unrelated `interviewService.ts` gap excluded). Prod deploy: `git merge --ff-only origin/main`, `docker compose -f docker-compose.production.yml up -d --build backend`. Post-boot, ran the exact fixed function inside the prod container against the exact title string that broke in production (`contentDispositionHeader('July 2026 - AI Systems Architect — recording')`) piped into a real `http.OutgoingMessage` — confirmed `SET_HEADER_OK`, no throw. 5-minute post-deploy log scan for `controller_error`: zero matches (down from the ~12 seen in the same window pre-fix).
  - Notes: This bug likely predates this session entirely (the `Content-Disposition` code was pre-existing, untouched by any of today's Zoom-migration PRs) — it was simply never exercised by a real download attempt with a non-ASCII title until today's recording backfill produced the first one. Worth a quick sanity check next time anyone touches Docs & Files: a PDF/file upload with an em-dash or emoji in its name would hit the identical bug.

### Operational alerting (BC #10099862873) — review fixes on feature/operational-alerting-p0 — 2026-07-20
- [x] Fixed 8 confirmed bugs found reviewing a prior session's "code-complete, tested, live-verified" claim before merge
  - Date: 2026-07-20
  - Session: CC-20260720-x4k9
  - What changed: BC #10099862873 (P0+P1 operational alerting, approved by Ali 2026-07-15) was pasted as a new ticket framed as a "reply task," but the real unresolved item was a 40-file/~2,500-line branch (`feature/operational-alerting-p0`, commit `df632072`, session `CC-20260716-x9qr`) with an existing comment claiming it was done and awaiting review. Checked out the branch (266 commits behind `staging` — merged clean, no conflicts, commit `9d1a2341`), then ran an 8-angle code review (line-by-line, removed-behavior, cross-file tracing, reuse/simplification/efficiency, altitude, CLAUDE.md conventions, each independently verified against actual source) before trusting the prior session's self-report. Found and fixed 8 real bugs, several of which directly undermined the ticket's own purpose:
    1. **`emitFailureEvent()` unhandled-rejection crash risk** (`apolloService.ts`, `ghlService.ts`, `ops/basecampClient.ts`, `synthflowService.ts`) — the lazy `await import('./aiEventService')` wasn't guarded by the helper's own try/catch (only the subsequent call was `.catch()`-guarded), so a rejected dynamic import was a true unhandled rejection with no `unhandledRejection` handler anywhere in `server.ts` — could crash the whole process on a routine external-API failure. Fixed by wrapping the entire helper body (import + call) in one try/catch with structured `error_class`-tagged logging, in all 4 files plus `authFailureLog.ts` (same silent-swallow pattern, different shape — `.then().catch(()=>{})` already guarded the import but logged nothing on failure).
    2. **`errorSpikeAlertService.ts` always-100%-failure-rate bug** — every watched event type is only ever emitted on the failure branch (no matching 'success' outcome exists anywhere for the same event_type), so `total` structurally always equalled `failed`, making the 50%/80% thresholds fire on any failure at all — 5 ordinary expired-JWT 401s would read as "100% error rate" and fire a CRITICAL alert (live Synthflow voice call per Ali's approved channel design), the opposite of "tune conservatively to avoid noise." Fixed by switching to absolute failure-count thresholds (`WARNING_COUNT=10`, `CRITICAL_COUNT=25`/hour) since there is no real denominator to compute a rate against — instrumenting a true success-path denominator would mean a DB write on every authenticated request and every external API call, a much larger unreviewed change of its own. Rewrote `evaluateErrorSpike()`'s signature and all 12 tests accordingly.
    3. **Silent cron-disable blind spot** (`cronInstrumentation.ts`) — wrapping previously-unconditional jobs (`PreviewStackReaper`, `StaleActionRecovery`, `AutonomousIngestInsights` in `schedulerService.ts`; 14 jobs in `aiOpsScheduler.ts`) in `instrumentCronJob()` made them newly conditional on an `AiAgent` row's `enabled`/`status`, and the skip produced zero log output — `cronHealthAlertService` only monitors `enabled: true` rows, so a disabled/mis-seeded row silently stopped a job with no alert, the exact "silently broken, nobody paged" pattern this ticket exists to close. Fixed by adding a structured `console.warn` on skip (kept scoped — did not redesign missed-run detection for the disabled-forever case, which would risk its own false-positive noise problem).
    4. **`incidentSubscriberBootstrap.ts` — no idempotency key on a newly-activated email path.** The dormant "cognitive incident" email fanout (intentionally separate from `alertService.ts` per the decision ticket — not a chokepoint-bypass bug) had zero dedup before this ticket registered it at boot for the first time, turning a previously-inert `fanOutIncident()` call (`projectRoutes.ts`'s manual dispatch route) into a real email send with nothing stopping a double-click/retry from sending twice. Added a 15-minute cooldown check against `IncidentDispatchLog` at the route's call site (no migration — reused the existing table).
    5. **`opsAlertSubscriptionSeed.ts` race condition** — manual `findOne`-then-`create`/`update` instead of Sequelize's `findOrCreate` (which the sibling `agentRegistrySeed.ts` already uses correctly for the same idempotent-seed shape), with no unique index backing it. Switched to `findOrCreate`. Did not add a migration for a unique index — that would invalidate the prior comment's "no DB migration required, pure app-code deploy" note; flagged as a follow-up worth a deliberate migration decision, not bundled silently into this pass.
    6. **`errorClassifier.ts` misclassification** — message-substring keyword checks (timeout/network) ran before the numeric HTTP status-code check, so a 401 with "network" in the message text was misclassified as `UpstreamUnavailable` instead of `AuthError`. Reordered: name → structured system error codes → HTTP status → message-substring fallback last.
    7. **No timeout on the Synthflow/GHL calls this diff instruments** — a hang on either call never tripped the new failure-classification/alerting logic at all. Added `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(15000)` to both; the existing catch blocks' `classifyError()` calls already map `AbortError` to `TimeoutError`, so this was the only piece missing.
    - Files: MODIFIED backend/src/services/{apolloService,ghlService,synthflowService,errorSpikeAlertService,cronInstrumentation,opsAlertSubscriptionSeed}.ts, backend/src/services/ops/basecampClient.ts, backend/src/middlewares/authFailureLog.ts, backend/src/utils/errorClassifier.ts, backend/src/routes/projectRoutes.ts; corresponding test files updated (`errorSpikeAlertService.test.ts` rewritten for count-based thresholds, `cronInstrumentation.test.ts`, `opsAlertSubscriptionSeed.test.ts`, `errorClassifier.test.ts`, `projectRoutes.test.ts` extended); NEW backend/src/services/__tests__/{synthflowTimeout,ghlTimeout}.test.ts.
  - Verification: every touched test file re-run individually and passing (errorSpikeAlertService 12/12, cronInstrumentation 8/8, opsAlertSubscriptionSeed 3/3, errorClassifier 11/11, projectRoutes 11/11 incl. 5 new dispatch-idempotency tests, synthflowTimeout 2/2, ghlTimeout 2/2). Backend `tsc --noEmit` clean after all fixes. Full backend suite re-run in background after the fixes (not the earlier, now-stale pre-fix run) — see follow-up note/next entry for the result once it lands.

- [x] Payment reconciliation silently skipped every $149 payment (students paid but stayed locked out of the portal)
  - Date: 2026-08-07
  - Session: CC-20260806-4b1e
  - What changed: `paymentReconciliationService.ts`'s `MINIMUM_FULL_PAYMENT_AMOUNT` was pinned at `199`, the old Monthly price. Pricing moved to **$149/mo billed annually** ($199 month-to-month) and the constant did not move with it, so the sweep's `p.Amount >= MINIMUM_FULL_PAYMENT_AMOUNT` filter dropped every $149 payment **before** the customer lookup — no match attempt, no flag, no error, nothing in the report. Affected students kept `payment_status='pending'`, so the portal treated them as not enrolled. Split it: the $50-deposit case now uses only $50 payments and still asserts skip, and a new regression test asserts a $149 payment IS scanned, reaches the customer lookup, and auto-reconciles with `amount === 149`.
  - Notes: Found via two student emails on 2026-08-06 — Hellen Muhonja ("still can't access the class on the portal", paid $149 on 08-04, PaySimple payment 155437561) and Firas Baidhani ("my account doesn't reflect my enrollment", paid $149 on 08-06, payment 155526546). Both verified against the live PaySimple API before any write. Both were then reconciled in production through the service's own `findMatchingEnrollment` + `reconcilePayment` functions (dry-run first, matched via email, then committed) rather than by hand-editing rows, so `seats_taken`, `portal_enabled`, `amount_paid` and the payment/customer id links were all set exactly as a normal reconciliation would. Verified after: both now `payment_status=paid`, `amount_paid=149.00`, `portal_enabled=t`. Also of note: `findCustomerByEmail` returns null for both of these customers because PaySimple does not honour its own `?email` filter (the guard in that function is working as documented) — so email-based lookup cannot be relied on as the discovery path here; the sweep is the mechanism that matters.

Badges pair a word with a distinct glyph (✔ ◐ ◆ ◷) so status survives colour-blindness and greyscale rather than relying on colour alone.

(3) `projectSync.ts`'s three bare `catch {}` blocks now distinguish 404 (API flag-gated off — still quiet) from anything else, emit a structured JSON error line with `error_class`, and notify an `onSyncFailure` subscriber so the UI can surface a retry (the surface itself is r0/STORY-003, not in this PR). - [x] "Watch recording" button was dead: an authenticated API path was being rendered as a plain link, so the tab landed on a 401
  - Date: 2026-08-09
  - Session: CC-20260806-4b1e
  - What changed: `LiveSession.recording_url` holds one of two different things. When a recording is ingested onto our own disk, `sessionRecordingService.ingestRecordingForSession` writes a RELATIVE, Bearer-gated API path (`/api/portal/community/rooms/:roomId/resources/:id/download`); when someone pastes an external provider link by hand it is an absolute URL. Every surviving consumer rendered it straight into `<a href target="_blank">`. For the absolute case that is fine; for the API path it is a plain browser navigation, which carries cookies but NOT the `Authorization: Bearer` header the portal holds client-side (`middlewares/participantAuth.ts` requires it), so the new tab got `401 {"error":"Authentication required"}` and the button appeared to do nothing. Added `openSessionRecording()` to `services/roomsApi.ts` next to the existing `downloadRoomResource()` (whose own comment already documented this exact trap): absolute URLs open directly, relative paths go through the authenticated `portalApi` client as a blob. The placeholder tab is opened synchronously BEFORE the await so the popup blocker does not eat it, with a download fallback if it is blocked, and the tab is closed and the error rethrown on failure. Wired into both broken consumers: `rooms/RoomPane.tsx` (the class banner button, which now shows an "Opening…" state and an inline error) and `PortalSessionsPage.tsx` (the Sessions-list "Recording" button, which had the identical defect and had not been reported yet).
  - Verification: Reproduced against production first, not inferred — the live `recording_url` for Session 5 (Week 2 Build Day, 2026-08-06) is the relative path, and an unauthenticated request to it returns exactly `401 {"error":"Authentication required"}`. The stored file is a valid MP4 (`ftypmp42` magic bytes, `video/mp4`) served by `res.sendFile`, which honours Range, so playback works once the request authenticates. Frontend `tsc --noEmit` 0 errors in `src/`; new `roomsApi.openSessionRecording.test.ts` 4/4 covering both branches, the synchronous-open ordering, and the failure path. CRA production build run locally with `CI=true` because the repo's "Frontend typecheck" CI job only runs `tsc` and is blind to CRA/ESLint production-build failures (the PR #742 landmine); diff deliberately contains no rule-specific `eslint-disable` comments and no unused imports.
  - Notes: The comment in `sessionRecordingService.ts` justifying the stored URL format points at `PortalSessionDetailPage.tsx` as "the existing Portal Watch Recording button" — **that file no longer exists in `main`**, so the comment's stated consumer is stale and should be re-pointed. Also worth knowing, and NOT addressed here: the Recordings tab on a per-session room reads only that room's resources, but recordings are attached to the persistent cohort room, so a session room shows "No recordings yet" while its banner offers the recording (both were visible in the same screenshot). That is correct scoping, not a bug, but it reads as a contradiction to a student. Separately, every file in `/app/uploads/room-recordings/` is between 30 KB and 1.2 MB, which is far too small to be a real 2-hour class recording, and Session 5's was created at 22:33 UTC, ~1 hour BEFORE that class started — the ingest pipeline is worth a look on its own.

### Student Build Pipeline: the F-1 fix didn't actually work — DROP INDEX vs DROP CONSTRAINT (2026-08-09)
- [x] **Caught my own merged fix failing against the real database, corrected it, applied it to prod, and added a post-condition check so this class of silent schema failure cannot recur**
  - Date: 2026-08-09
  - Session: CC-20260809-b7k2
  - What changed: Immediately after PR #1281 merged, I ran its DDL against production to unblock persistence without a mid-afternoon backend restart, and it **failed**: `ERROR: cannot drop index student_tasks_unique_req_key because constraint student_tasks_unique_req_key on table student_tasks requires it`. Sequelize's `unique: true` in a model's `indexes` array creates a **CONSTRAINT**, not a bare index, and a constraint-backed index cannot be dropped with `DROP INDEX`. The merged statement was `DROP INDEX IF EXISTS student_tasks_unique_req_key` — and because `ensureStudentTaskMergeSchema()` wraps every statement in a `try/catch` that only `console.warn`s, it would have failed **silently at every boot**, logged one line as "stmt skipped", and left the constraint in place. The fix I shipped would not have fixed anything. My unit tests did not catch it because they mock the models entirely — they exercise `importProject`'s control flow, never the DDL. Corrected in follow-up: `ALTER TABLE student_tasks DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS student_tasks_unique_req_key` first (which removes the backing index too), then the bare `DROP INDEX IF EXISTS` for any DB where it exists without a constraint; both `IF EXISTS`, so the pair is idempotent. Then addressed the root enabler rather than just the instance: added a **post-condition check** after the statement loop that queries `pg_constraint` and `pg_indexes` for the name and, if either still reports it, emits a structured `level:error` line with `error_class: SchemaInvariantViolation`, the impact ("student build imports will abort on the first duplicate requirement_key") and the exact remedial SQL. "It didn't throw" is not evidence a best-effort statement took effect — the check asserts the outcome.
  - Verification: Applied to production directly and confirmed by re-query: `student_tasks_unique_req_key` is now absent from BOTH `pg_indexes` and `pg_constraint` on `student_tasks`; the correct partial unique `student_tasks_unique_story` remains; all 3 existing task rows intact (no data touched — dropping a uniqueness constraint only widens what is permitted). **Production persistence is unblocked as of this entry.** Backend `tsc --noEmit` (TypeScript 5.7.3): 1 error, the known `@anthropic-ai/sdk` worktree artifact; zero in `server.ts`.
  - Notes: The honest lesson is that PR #1281's verification was weaker than it read. It claimed a regression test that "reproduces the original failure" — it reproduces the *application-level* failure (a simulated unique violation aborting the import) but never the *schema* change, so a wrong DDL passed every gate: 4 green CI checks, 27 green tests, two clean typechecks. Mocked-model tests cannot verify DDL, and nothing in this repo currently runs migrations against a real Postgres in CI. Worth considering a migration smoke test as follow-up work; not attempted here. Prod DB and the code are now consistent, and the post-check makes a future divergence loud on the next boot rather than invisible.

### Student Build Pipeline: GitHub sync + document architecture plan (SBP-GH-v1) (2026-08-09)
- [x] **Ran the pilot end to end on Ali's account, found the prompts reference files that exist for nobody, and specified the GitHub-as-system-of-record architecture that fixes it**
  - Date: 2026-08-09
  - Session: CC-20260809-b7k2
  - What changed: Added `docs/BUILD_PIPELINE_GITHUB_SYNC.md` (SBP-GH-v1). **The defect Ali caught:** the story prompts I generated open with `## Read this first` pointing at `./docs/REQUIREMENTS.md`, `./docs/stories/STORY-nnn.md` and `./CLAUDE.md`. Those resolve on Ali's machine because he has this repo; for a student they resolve to nothing, because nothing writes them. I had specified FR-021 (materialize docs into the workspace repo) and then generated prompts that assume FR-021 was already built. A student pasting that prompt gets four failed reads and an agent that believes it has context it does not — worse than no context. Verified the GitHub layer has never run for real: every `github_connections` row in prod is test data (`octocat/Hello-World`), so nothing has ever written to a student repo. The plan resolves Ali's stated preference (docs in GitHub, surfaced on our site) into an architecture: **GitHub is the system of record, Postgres holds a rebuildable projection**, matching the existing training.colaberry.com KB-projection pattern and CLAUDE.md's one-owner-per-artifact discipline. Specifies the repo layout (`docs/**`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.colaberry/{plan,manifest,progress}.json`), both sync directions, a path allowlist so platform writes can never touch student code, hash-based conflict detection that never silently overwrites a student's edits (diverged → write `.generated.md` + portal banner + keep-mine/take-generated), a no-repo fallback that inlines context instead of emitting unresolvable paths, and **FR-032: prompt assembly asserts every path it references against the manifest** — the single check that would have caught this defect. Adds 8 requirements (FR-025..FR-032). Also specifies deriving story progress from repo evidence (commit messages matching `STORY-\d+`, acceptance checkboxes in the story files) rather than a self-reported checkbox, which is what finally makes the 4-state advance — it has never moved once in production. Dashboard section enumerates 8 panels, all derivable from plan + projection with no new capture. Proposes renaming "builds" to "projects" in the UI while keeping "release"/"story" (real terms students should graduate speaking). **Extended mid-session on Ali's direction** with the work-surface design (FR-033..FR-036): the task card drops to ONE primary action (**Open**) with tool choice moved into the drawer after the student has read the story; a full-page workspace at `/portal/projects/:projectId/stories/:storyId` at Classroom scale, with a wide right rail carrying a story-seeded `PortalMentorChat` agent plus repo and checks panels; and — the substantive one — **mark-done is gated on GitHub evidence**, disabled until the repo shows a provisioned workspace, commits referencing the story id, and every acceptance checkbox ticked in `docs/stories/STORY-nnn.md`. The checks panel names the failing check and its remedy rather than greying out a button. Because a hard gate with no escape is a trap, FR-034 requires three releases: on-demand re-check (never make a student wait on our webhook), mentor review with a recorded override (never self-override), and a `evidence: document` story type for stories with no code outcome. **Sync mechanism decided (§5.2, FR-041..FR-043):** webhook primary with reconciliation polling as a safety net. Receiver verifies GitHub's HMAC over the RAW body bytes and returns **202 immediately** doing no work in the request (reusing `buildPlanWebhookController.ts`'s existing `verifyHmacSignature`/`rawBody` pattern rather than writing a second one), then enqueues the sync on the bounded queue; pushes authored by the platform bot are ignored so our own document write cannot trigger a sync loop. `last_synced_sha` persists per project and every sync records commit, changed files, outcome and timestamp. A 15–60 min reconciler repairs SHA mismatches under an advisory lock, because **GitHub does not guarantee redelivery of a failed webhook** — without it, one delivery lost during a backend restart leaves a build permanently stale and a student's mark-done gate stuck closed through no fault of their own. The reconciler uses conditional requests (`ETag`/`If-None-Match`); an authenticated `304 Not Modified` does not count against the primary rate limit, which is what keeps reconciling a whole cohort every 15 minutes nearly free. Noted why a GitHub Actions workflow or a host's native Git integration does not substitute here: the payload we need is build progress (which commits touch which story, which acceptance boxes are ticked), not a deploy trigger. **Decisions locked by Ali the same session (§4.1):** repo provisioning is **mandatory** (a fourth wizard step, before Confirm & build) and there is **one repo per project**, not per student. The second is a schema change: `github_connections.enrollment_id` is currently `UNIQUE`, which structurally forbids it — so that unique is dropped to a plain index and `UNIQUE (project_id)` added, with the service re-keyed to take `projectId` and verify ownership through the enrollment. Verified the migration is clean before proposing it: production holds 11 `github_connections` rows and **zero** are real platform-provisioned workspace repos (none match `ColaberryIntern/student-workspace-%` — they are `octocat/Hello-World` test rows plus one `AI_Pathway`), so there is nothing to preserve and this is cheaper to do now than after the first real repo exists. Repo naming moves from the bare-UUID `student-workspace-<enrollmentId>` to `<project-slug>-<first8 of projectId>` since the repo becomes the student's portfolio artifact. Mandatory provisioning is specified so it cannot become brittle: GitHub username validated against the API before provisioning (current code checks format only), no-account and provisioning-failure paths keep the intake saved and resumable via an `awaiting_repo` state, and provisioning runs through the same bounded queue as generation so a cohort starting together cannot exhaust the platform token's secondary rate limit. Adds FR-037..FR-040. That gating is what makes the page's existing promise — "completing tasks advances your requirements toward verified" — true rather than a self-report.
  - Verification: Pilot ran end to end first, and the plan is written against what it actually produced. Architect: brief → 15,387 words / 7 chapters / 110,637 chars in ~6 min, with its quality gate visibly firing (`Retrying chapter 1 (score 57<70, words 1331<1750)`). Decomposition committed project `248d9d63` to Ali's active enrollment: 5 releases, 12 stories, 18 requirements, 13 capabilities, every story carrying a 2,994–3,529-char prompt. Confirmed served by the real route — minted a participant JWT in-container and called `GET /api/portal/projects/active`: 200, 5 lists, 12 tasks, 12/12 with a >1,200-char prompt. **This is the first project in production history holding both requirements and tasks** (`projects_with_both_reqs_and_tasks` = 1; 8 projects have held requirements since April with zero tasks).

- [x] Fix an idempotency defect in authorTimelineCard caught by running the Week 1 seeders twice against production
  - Date: 2026-08-09
  - Session: CC-20260806-b4k2
  - What changed: after deploying the Week 1 content, the standing "run it twice" check showed two of three cards correctly reporting `already-current` with no write, but the **Claude Code 101** card reporting `applied` on every run. Root cause: `authorTimelineCard.same()` compared values with a plain `JSON.stringify`, and Postgres **`jsonb` does not preserve object key order**. That card is the only one of the three that writes a nested object (`meta.course`), so its authored literal `{name,url,sections}` came back from the DB reordered, compared unequal to itself, and rewrote the card — churning `content_at` — on every single run. Fixed by canonicalising key order recursively before comparing (`canon()`), while deliberately preserving array order, since question order on a card is meaningful. This is an idempotency violation, which this repo classifies as a production defect rather than a nit, so it is fixed rather than noted.
  - Verification: new `backend/src/scripts/lib/__tests__/authorTimelineCard.test.ts`, **7/7 passing**, opening with a test that reproduces the exact original break (the authored `course` literal vs the same object with jsonb's key order) and also covering nested depth, real content changes still reading as different, array order staying significant, key order inside array elements, and primitive/null/undefined handling. Backend `tsc --noEmit` clean — zero errors in the changed file, only the pre-existing unrelated `@anthropic-ai/sdk` gap. Re-verified against **production** after redeploy: all three cards now report `already-current` on a second consecutive run.

### Student Build Pipeline: decomposer generator T0 (2026-08-10)

Splitting them is what makes the part that decides *what the model is told* unit-testable with no network, which matters because the pilot proved that is where the quality lives. The system prompt encodes every lesson the pilot produced: the brief is GROUND TRUTH and outranks the generated expansion; anti-invention rules naming the exact things it hallucinated (Stripe, PayPal, HIPAA, an HR integration); `CONSTRAINT` explained as context-not-work-item with the concrete failure it prevents ("System connects to Postgres for data access"); vertical-slice and no-scaffold rules; release spread; walking-skeleton r0 whose demo shows the guarantee holding rather than a happy path. Failure behaviour per CLAUDE.md Failure-First: explicit 240s timeout, SDK retries capped at 1, schema-invalid output retried exactly once (with the rejection reason fed back) and then a clean typed failure — `ConfigError`, `UpstreamTimeout`, `UpstreamError`, `EmptyResponse`, `ContractViolation`. Timeouts are classified separately from other upstream errors so a caller can distinguish "retry later" from "this is broken". Generation deliberately does NOT gate: the caller runs `gatePlan` and decides, keeping generation and judgement separable.

Failure paths each have a test: retry-once-then-succeed, the retry carries the rejection reason, hard failure never makes a third call, a well-formed-but-empty plan is rejected rather than returned, timeout vs upstream-error classification, and empty response. Observability is tested too — the success line carries the correlation id and counts, the failure line carries an `error_class`, and a secret planted in the brief is asserted **never** to appear in any log line.
